title.zh: 卷一百一十 列傳第四十八: 楊雲翼 趙秉文 韓玉 馮璧 李獻甫 雷淵 程震
title.en: Volume 110 Biographies 48: Yang Yunyi, Zhao Bingwen, Han Yu, Feng Bi, Li Xianfu, Lei Yuan, Cheng Zhen
title.raw: 卷一百一十 列傳第四十八: 楊雲翼 趙秉文 韓玉 馮璧 李獻甫 雷淵 程震 Volume 110 Biographies 48: Yang Yunyi, Zhao Bingwen, Han Yu, Feng Bi, Li Xianfu, Lei Yuan, Cheng Zhen

sentences.zh: 楊雲翼

translations.literal: Yang Yunyi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunyi

sentences.zh: 楊雲翼，字之美，其先贊皇檀山人，六代祖忠，客平定之樂平縣，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Yang Yunyi, styled Zhi Mei, his ancestors were from Tan Mountain in Zanhuang; in the sixth generation his ancestor Zhong lodged as a guest in Leping County in Pingding, and thereupon made his home.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunyi, whose style name was Zhi Mei, came from Tan Mountain in Zanhuang. Six generations back, his ancestor Zhong settled in Leping County in Pingding as a guest resident, and the family made its home there.

sentences.zh: 曾祖青、祖鬱、考恆，皆贈官於朝。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qing, grandfather Yu, and father Heng were all granted posthumous offices at court.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qing, grandfather Yu, and father Heng were all posthumously granted offices at court.

sentences.zh: 雲翼天資穎悟，初學語輒畫地作字，日誦數千言。

translations.literal: Yunyi was gifted and perceptive by nature; as soon as he began to learn speech he would trace characters on the ground, and each day recited several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi was exceptionally bright by nature. As soon as he learned to speak he would trace characters on the ground, and he recited several thousand words a day.

sentences.zh: 登明昌五年進士第一，詞賦亦中乙科，特授承務郎、應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: He placed first in the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Mingchang; in the cifu examination he also passed the second rank, and was specially appointed Cheng Wu Lang and Hanlin Attendant for Documentation.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place in the jinshi examination of the fifth year of Mingchang and also passed the second rank in the rhapsody examination. He was specially appointed as Cheng Wu Lang and Hanlin Attendant for Documentation.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，出為陝西東路兵馬都總管判官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chengan he went out as judicial officer to the Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs on the Shaanxi Eastern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chengan he was posted as judicial officer under the Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs on the Shaanxi Eastern Circuit.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，召為太學博士，遷太常寺丞，兼翰林修撰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy, promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and concurrently made Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taihe he was summoned to serve as Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while also serving as Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 七年，簽上京、東京等路按察司事，因召見，章宗咨以當世之務，稱旨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he signed matters for the Surveillance Commission on the Shangjing, Dongjing, and other circuits; because of a summons for audience, Zhangzong consulted him on affairs of the age, and he met with approval.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he handled affairs for the Surveillance Commission on the Shangjing, Dongjing, and other circuits. Summoned to audience, he answered Zhangzong's questions on current affairs to the emperor's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 大安元年，翰林承旨張行簡薦其材，且精術數，召授提點司天臺，兼翰林修撰，俄兼禮部郎中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daan, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Zhang Xingjian recommended his talent and that he was skilled in numerology; he was summoned and appointed Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, concurrently Hanlin Compiler, and shortly thereafter concurrently Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daan, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Zhang Xingjian recommended him for his ability and his mastery of numerology. He was summoned and appointed Director of the Directorate of Astronomy while retaining his post as Hanlin Compiler, and soon afterward was also made Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 崇慶元年，以病歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongqing he returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongqing he retired home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，有司上官簿，宣宗閱之，記其姓名，起授前職，兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou the relevant offices presented the official register upward; Xuanzong reviewed it, noted his name, and reappointed him to his former post, concurrently Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou the authorities submitted the official register. Xuanzong read through it, noted Yunyi's name, and recalled him to his former post while also making him Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉禮部侍郎，兼提點司天臺。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites while continuing to direct the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 四年，大元及西夏兵入鄜延，潼關失守，朝議以兵部尚書蒲察阿裏不孫為副元帥以禦之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Great Yuan and Western Xia troops entered Fuyan; Tong Pass was lost. The court deliberated making Minister of War Pucha Alibusun deputy commander-in-chief to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Yuan and Western Xia forces entered Fuyan and Tong Pass fell. The court decided to appoint Minister of War Pucha Alibusun deputy commander-in-chief to meet the invasion.

sentences.zh: 雲翼言其人言浮於實，必誤大事。

translations.literal: Yunyi said that this man's words exceeded his substance and would surely ruin a great affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi said the man's talk outran his substance and that he was bound to ruin the campaign.

sentences.zh: 不聽，後果敗。

translations.literal: They did not heed him; afterward he was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not listen, and defeat followed as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 興定元年六月，遷翰林侍講學士，兼修國史，知集賢院事，兼前職，詔曰：「官制入三品者例外除，以卿遇事敢言，議論忠讜，故特留之。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Xingding he was moved to Hanlin Attendant Lecturer, concurrently Compiler of the National History, Administrator of the Hall of Assembled Talents, and his former posts; an edict said: 'By the official regulations those who enter the third rank are removed from other appointments, but because you speak boldly on affairs you encounter and your opinions are loyal and forthright, you are specially retained.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Xingding he was promoted to Hanlin Attendant Lecturer, made Compiler of the National History and Administrator of the Hall of Assembled Talents while keeping his other posts. An edict read: 'Regulations require that officials who reach the third rank give up concurrent appointments, but because you speak boldly when matters arise and your counsel is loyal and candid, you are specially allowed to keep them.'

sentences.zh: 時右丞相高琪當國，人有請榷油者，高琪主之甚力，詔集百官議，戶部尚書高夔等二十六人同聲曰：「可。」

translations.literal: At that time the Right Chancellor Gao Qi held power. Someone requested a government monopoly on oil; Gao Qi advocated it vigorously. An edict summoned all officials to deliberate; Minister of Revenue Gao Kui and twenty-six others in one voice said: 'It may be done.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Right Chancellor Gao Qi dominated the government. When someone proposed a state monopoly on oil, Gao Qi pushed it hard. The emperor ordered all officials to debate the matter. Minister of Revenue Gao Kui and twenty-six others spoke as one: 'It should be done.'

sentences.zh: 雲翼獨與趙秉文、時戩等數人以為不可，議遂格。

translations.literal: Yunyi alone, with Zhao Bingwen, Shi E, and several others, held that it could not be done, and the proposal was thereupon blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi alone, together with Zhao Bingwen, Shi E, and a few others, argued that it should not be done, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 高琪後以事譴之，雲翼不恤也。

translations.literal: Gao Qi later censured him over the affair, but Yunyi paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi later punished him over the affair, but Yunyi took no notice.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜禮部尚書，兼職如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Minister of Rites, his concurrent posts remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Minister of Rites while keeping his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 三年，築京師子城，役兵民數萬，夏秋之交病者相籍，雲翼提舉醫藥，躬自調護，多所全濟。

translations.literal: In the third year the inner city of the capital was built; tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians were conscripted. At the turn of summer and autumn the sick lay pressed against one another. Yunyi supervised medical care, personally attending and treating them, and many were fully saved.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year work began on the capital's inner wall, conscripting tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians. At the height of summer sickness spread through the camps. Yunyi took charge of medical relief, tended the sick himself, and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 四年，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 凡軍興以來，入粟補官及以戰功遷授者，事定之後，有司苛為程式，或小有不合輒罷去，雲翼奏曰：「賞罰國之大信，此輩宜從寬錄，以勸將來。」

translations.literal: Ever since the armies were raised, those who bought office with grain and those promoted for military merit—after affairs were settled the offices harshly applied regulations, and if there was the slightest nonconformity they were dismissed at once. Yunyi memorialized: 'Rewards and punishments are the great trust of the state; these men ought to be recorded leniently, to encourage those who come after.'
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, men who had bought office with grain contributions or won promotion through military merit found that once fighting ended, the bureaucracy applied the rules harshly and dismissed them for the slightest irregularity. Yunyi submitted a memorial: 'Rewards and punishments are the foundation of state credibility. These men should be treated leniently so as to encourage others in the future.'

sentences.zh: 是年九月，上召雲翼及戶部尚書夔、翰林學士秉文于內殿，皆賜坐，問以講和之策，或以力戰為言，上俯首不樂，雲翼徐以《孟子》事大、事小之說解之，且曰：「今日奚計哉，使生靈息肩，則社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year the emperor summoned Yunyi, Minister of Revenue Kui, and Hanlin Academician Bingwen to the inner hall, all granted seats, and asked about a policy of peace. Some spoke of fighting with force; the emperor bowed his head, displeased. Yunyi slowly explained it with Mencius's doctrine of serving the great and serving the small, and said: 'What is there to calculate today? If the people may rest their shoulders, that is the blessing of the altars of soil and grain.'
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year the emperor summoned Yunyi, Minister of Revenue Kui, and Hanlin Academician Bingwen to the inner hall and had them seated. He asked their views on making peace. Some urged continued fighting, and the emperor looked down, plainly displeased. Yunyi gently explained the matter using Mencius's distinction between serving a greater power and serving a lesser one, and said: 'What is there to calculate today? If the people can lay down their burdens, that will be the state's greatest blessing.'

sentences.zh: 上色乃和。

translations.literal: The emperor's countenance thereupon became harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression softened.

sentences.zh: 十一月，改御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was changed to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 宗室承立權參知政事，行尚書省事於京兆，大臣言其不法，詔雲翼就鞫之，獄成，廷奏曰：「承立所坐皆細事，不足問。

translations.literal: The imperial clansman Chengli held acting office as Vice Grand Councilor and administered the Secretariat affairs at Jingzhao. Great ministers said he acted unlawfully; an edict ordered Yunyi to go and try him. When the case was complete he reported at court: 'Chengli's offenses are all minor matters, not worth inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Chengli served as acting Vice Grand Councilor and ran the Secretariat at Jingzhao. Senior ministers accused him of misconduct, and the emperor ordered Yunyi to investigate. When the trial concluded, Yunyi reported at court: 'Chengli's offenses are all trifles, not worth pursuing.

sentences.zh: 向大兵掠平涼以西，數州皆破，承立坐擁強兵，瞻望不進。

translations.literal: Recently the great army plundered west of Pingliang and several prefectures were all broken; Chengli sat holding strong troops and looked on without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy swept west of Pingliang and overran several prefectures, Chengli sat on a strong force and watched without advancing.

sentences.zh: 鄜延帥臣完顏合達以孤城當兵沖，屢立戰績。

translations.literal: The Fuyan commander Wanyan Hedai, with a lone city facing the brunt of the army, repeatedly established battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyan commander Wanyan Hedai held a isolated city against the main enemy thrust and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 其功如此，而承立之罪如彼，願陛下明其功罪以誅賞之，則天下知所勸懲矣。

translations.literal: His merit is thus, while Chengli's crime is as that; I wish Your Majesty would clarify merit and crime to punish and reward them, then all under Heaven would know what to encourage and what to restrain.
translations.idiomatic: Here is merit of one kind and guilt of another. I ask Your Majesty to weigh their deeds clearly and reward or punish accordingly, so that the realm will know what conduct to encourage and what to forbid.

sentences.zh: 自余小失，何足追咎。」

translations.literal: As for the remaining minor faults, how are they worth pursuing to blame?'
translations.idiomatic: As for his other petty faults, they are hardly worth pursuing.'

sentences.zh: 承立由是免官，合達遂掌機務。

translations.literal: Chengli was thereby dismissed from office, and Hedai thereupon took charge of key affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chengli was dismissed from office as a result, and Hedai was put in charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 哀宗即位，首命雲翼攝太常卿，尋拜翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Aizong took the throne he first ordered Yunyi to act as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; shortly he was appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Aizong ascended the throne he first made Yunyi acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then appointed him Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 正大二年二月，複為禮部尚書，兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhengda he again became Minister of Rites, concurrently Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Zhengda he was again appointed Minister of Rites and Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 詔集百官議省費，雲翼曰：「省費事小，戶部司農足以辦之。

translations.literal: An edict gathered all officials to deliberate on reducing expenses. Yunyi said: 'Reducing expenses is a small matter; the Ministry of Revenue and the Directorate of Agriculture are sufficient to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all officials to discuss cutting expenses. Yunyi said: 'Economizing is a minor matter that the Ministry of Revenue and the Directorate of Agriculture can handle on their own.

sentences.zh: 樞密專制軍政，蔑視尚書。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs monopolizes military administration and looks down on the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs monopolizes military administration and treats the Secretariat with contempt.

sentences.zh: 尚書出政之地，政無大小，皆當總領。

translations.literal: The Secretariat is the place from which government issues forth; affairs great and small ought all to be overseen in chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat is where government issues forth, and affairs great and small ought all to come under its oversight.

sentences.zh: 今軍旅大事，社稷系焉，宰相乃不得預聞，欲使利病兩不相蔽得乎。」

translations.literal: Now on great military affairs on which the altars of soil and grain depend, the chief ministers cannot even hear beforehand—can you wish that benefit and harm will not each obscure the other?'
translations.idiomatic: Yet on great military matters on which the fate of the state depends, the chief ministers are not even informed in advance. How can benefit and harm be weighed without each side hiding from the other?'

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 明年，設益政院，雲翼為選首，每召見賜坐而不名。

translations.literal: The next year the Bureau for Promoting Governance was established; Yunyi was chosen as its head. Each time he was summoned for audience he was granted a seat and not called by name.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Bureau for Promoting Governance was established with Yunyi as its head. Whenever he was summoned, he was given a seat and addressed without using his personal name.

sentences.zh: 時講《尚書》，雲翼為言帝王之學不必如經生分章析句，但知為國大綱足矣。

translations.literal: At that time they lectured on the Documents; Yunyi said that the learning of emperors and kings need not be like classicists who split chapters and analyze sentences—it is enough merely to know the great outline of governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: While lecturing on the Documents, Yunyi said that a ruler's learning need not follow the classicists' habit of parsing every chapter and line. Knowing the great principles of governing the state is enough.

sentences.zh: 因舉「任賢」「去邪」、「與治同道」「與亂同事」、「有言逆於汝心」「有言遜於汝志」等數條，一皆本於正心誠意，敷繹詳明。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cited several passages such as 'appoint the worthy' and 'remove the depraved,' 'walk the same path as order' and 'share the same work as disorder,' 'words that go against your mind' and 'words that yield to your will'—each rooted in rectifying the mind and making intentions sincere, and he unfolded and explained them in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited such passages as 'appoint the worthy' and 'remove the wicked,' 'walk the same path as good government' and 'share the work of disorder,' and 'words that go against your mind' and 'words that flatter your wishes.' Each he traced back to rectifying the mind and making the will sincere, and he explained them at length with great clarity.

sentences.zh: 上聽忘倦。

translations.literal: The emperor listened and forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened without tiring.

sentences.zh: 尋進《龜鑑萬年錄》、《聖學》、《聖孝》之類凡二十篇。

translations.literal: Shortly he presented works such as Records of the Tortoise Mirror for Ten Thousand Years, Sacred Learning, and Sacred Filial Piety—twenty pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he presented twenty works including Records of the Tortoise Mirror for Ten Thousand Years, Sacred Learning, and Sacred Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 當時朝士，廷議之際多不盡言，顧望依違，浸以成俗。

translations.literal: At that time court gentlemen, when deliberating at court, often did not speak fully; they looked about and wavered, and this gradually became custom.
translations.idiomatic: At that time court officials often held back at deliberations, looking about and hedging until evasion became the custom.

sentences.zh: 一日，經筵畢，因言：「人臣有事君之禮，有事君之義。

translations.literal: One day, when the classics lecture was finished, he spoke thus: 'A subject has the ritual of serving the ruler, and the duty of serving the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: One day, after the classics lecture ended, he said: 'A subject owes the ruler both ritual observance and loyal duty.

sentences.zh: 禮，不敢齒君之路馬，蹴其芻者有罰，入君門則趨，見君之幾杖則起，君命召不俟駕而行，受命不宿於家，是皆事君之禮，人臣所當盡者也。

translations.literal: Ritual: not daring to rank alongside the ruler's road horses; kicking their fodder is punishable; entering the ruler's gate one hurries; seeing the ruler's armrest or staff one rises; when the ruler commands a summons one goes without waiting for the carriage to be yoked; receiving a command one does not lodge overnight at home—these are all rituals of serving the ruler that subjects ought fully to perform.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual means not daring to stand beside the ruler's horses on the road, punishing anyone who kicks their fodder, hurrying through the palace gate, rising at sight of the ruler's staff, setting out at once when summoned without waiting for the carriage to be readied, and not spending the night at home after receiving a command. These are the rituals of serving the ruler, and every subject should observe them.

sentences.zh: 然國家之利害，生民之休戚，一一陳之，則向所謂禮者特虛器耳。

translations.literal: Yet if the benefit and harm of the state and the weal and woe of the people are set forth one by one, then what was called ritual is only an empty vessel.
translations.idiomatic: But unless one sets forth the state's interests and the people's welfare point by point, all those observances are empty forms.

sentences.zh: 君曰可，而有否者獻其否；

translations.literal: When the ruler says it may be done, yet there is what may not be done, one presents what may not be done;
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler says yes but there is reason to say no, one must present the no;

sentences.zh: 君曰否，而有可者獻其可。

translations.literal: when the ruler says it may not be done, yet there is what may be done, one presents what may be done.
translations.idiomatic: when the ruler says no but there is reason to say yes, one must present the yes.

sentences.zh: 言有不從，雖引裾、折檻、斷鞅、軔輪有不恤焉者。

translations.literal: If words are not followed, even though one grasps the robe, breaks the balustrade, severs the saddle flap, or blocks the wheel hub—there are those who do not shrink from it.
translations.idiomatic: If counsel goes unheeded, there are those who will grasp the ruler's robe, break the balustrade, seize the bridle, or block the chariot wheel without flinching.

sentences.zh: 當是時也，姑徇事君之虛禮，而不知事君之大義，國家何賴焉。」

translations.literal: At such a time, if one merely follows the empty ritual of serving the ruler and does not know the great duty of serving the ruler, on what can the state rely?'
translations.idiomatic: If in such times one observes only the empty rituals of service and ignores the great duty owed the ruler, what can the state rely on?'

sentences.zh: 上變色曰：「非卿，朕不聞此言。」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said: 'Were it not for you, We would not have heard these words.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed. He said: 'Had it not been for you, I would never have heard this said.'

sentences.zh: 雲翼嘗患風痹，至是稍愈，上親問愈之之方，對曰：「但治心耳。

translations.literal: Yunyi had suffered from wind paralysis; by this time he had improved somewhat. The emperor personally asked the method of curing it. He replied: 'Only cure the mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi had long suffered from rheumatic paralysis, and by now he was somewhat better. The emperor personally asked how to cure it. He answered: 'Only by curing the mind.

sentences.zh: 心和則邪氣不幹，治國亦然，人君先正其心，則朝廷百官莫不一於正矣。」

translations.literal: When the mind is harmonious, evil qi does not interfere; governing the state is likewise—if the ruler first rectifies his mind, then the hundred officials of the court will all be unified in rectitude.'
translations.idiomatic: When the mind is at peace, no malign influence can touch the body. Governing the state works the same way: if the ruler first sets his mind right, every official at court will follow suit.'

sentences.zh: 上矍然，知其為醫諫也。

translations.literal: The emperor started awake, knowing that this was medical remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started, recognizing this as medical counsel directed at the state.

sentences.zh: 夏人既通好，遣其徽猷閣學士李弁來議互市，往返不能決，朝廷以雲翼往議乃定。

translations.literal: After the Xia people had made peace, they sent their Academician of the Hall of Splendid Teachings Li Bian to negotiate mutual markets; back and forth they could not decide. The court sent Yunyi to negotiate and then it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: After peace with the Western Xia, they sent Academician Li Bian of the Hall of Splendid Teachings to negotiate border trade, but talks went back and forth without resolution until the court sent Yunyi to negotiate and the terms were settled.

sentences.zh: 五年卒，年五十有九，諡文獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged fifty-nine; his posthumous title was Wenuian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year at the age of fifty-nine and was given the posthumous title Wenuian.

sentences.zh: 雲翼天性雅重，自律甚嚴，其待人則寬，與人交分一定，死生禍福不少變。

translations.literal: Yunyi was refined and weighty by nature, very strict in disciplining himself, yet lenient in treating others; in friendship his measure was fixed, and through death, life, fortune, or misfortune he changed little.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Yunyi was refined and dignified, stern with himself but generous toward others. Once he fixed the terms of a friendship, he changed little whether in life or death, fortune or misfortune.

sentences.zh: 其於國家之事，知無不言。

translations.literal: Regarding affairs of the state, what he knew he did not fail to speak.
translations.idiomatic: On matters of state he spoke whenever he had knowledge to offer.

sentences.zh: 貞祐中，主兵者不能外禦而欲取償于宋，故頻歲南伐。

translations.literal: In Zhenyou, those in charge of the armies could not defend outwardly yet wished to take compensation from Song, and therefore for successive years they campaigned south.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyou, the men in charge of the armies could not hold the northern frontier yet sought compensation from Song, and so they launched southern campaigns year after year.

sentences.zh: 有言之者，不謂之與宋為地，則疑與之有謀。

translations.literal: Whoever spoke of it was either said to be making common cause with Song, or suspected of plotting with them.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who spoke up was either accused of colluding with Song or suspected of secret dealings with them.

sentences.zh: 至於宰執，他事無不言者，獨南伐則一語不敢及。

translations.literal: As for the chief ministers, on other matters there was none who did not speak, but on the southern campaigns alone not one dared touch a word.
translations.idiomatic: Even the chief ministers, who spoke freely on every other matter, dared not utter a single word about the southern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 雲翼乃建言曰：「國家之慮，不在於未得淮南之前，而在城既得淮南之後。

translations.literal: Yunyi thereupon offered counsel: 'The state's concern lies not before gaining Huainan, but after the walls have already gained Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi submitted a memorial: 'The state's worry lies not in failing to take Huainan, but in what happens after Huainan is taken.

sentences.zh: 蓋淮南平則江之北盡為戰地，進而爭利於舟楫之間，恐勁弓良馬有不得騁者矣。

translations.literal: For if Huainan is pacified, then all north of the Yangzi becomes battleground; advancing to contend for advantage among boats and oars, I fear strong bows and fine horses may have no place to run free.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huainan falls, everything north of the Yangzi becomes a battleground. Fighting for advantage on the water, our strong bows and fine horses may have no room to show their worth.

sentences.zh: 彼若扼江為屯，潛師於淮以斷餉道，或決水以瀦淮南之地，則我軍何以善其後乎。」

translations.literal: If they choke the river with encampments, send troops secretly along the Huai to cut supply routes, or breach the dikes to flood Huainan, how will our army make a good aftermath?'
translations.idiomatic: If they block the river with camps, move troops secretly along the Huai to cut our supply lines, or breach the dikes to flood Huainan, how will our army recover afterward?'

sentences.zh: 及時全倡議南伐，宣宗以問朝臣，雲翼曰：「朝臣率皆諛辭，天下有治有亂，國勢有弱有強，今但言治而不言亂，言強而不言弱，言勝而不言負，此議論所以偏也。

translations.literal: When Shi Quan advocated a southern campaign, Xuanzong questioned the court gentlemen. Yunyi said: 'Court gentlemen are all flattery; all under Heaven has order and has disorder, the state's power has weakness and has strength. Now they speak only of order and not of disorder, only of strength and not of weakness, only of victory and not of defeat—this is why deliberation is biased.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Quan urged a southern campaign, Xuanzong asked the court for their views. Yunyi said: 'The ministers speak only to flatter. The realm knows order and disorder, and a state knows strength and weakness. Yet they speak only of order, not disorder; only of strength, not weakness; only of victory, not defeat. That is why their counsel is one-sided.

sentences.zh: 臣請兩言之。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to speak of both sides.
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to speak of both sides.

sentences.zh: 夫將有事于宋者，非貪其土地也，第恐西北有警而南又綴之，則我三面受敵矣，故欲我師乘勢先動，以阻其進。

translations.literal: As for wishing to act against Song, it is not from greed for their land; it is only fear that if there is alarm in the northwest and the south also presses, then we will receive enemies on three sides. Therefore they wish our army to seize the momentum and move first, to obstruct their advance.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to act against Song are not greedy for territory. They fear that if trouble breaks out in the northwest while the south also presses us, we will face enemies on three sides. They want our armies to strike first and block Song's advance.

sentences.zh: 借使宋人失淮，且不敢來，此戰勝之利也。

translations.literal: Even supposing the Song lose the Huai and moreover dare not come, this is the benefit of victory in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Song lost the Huai and dared not advance, that would be the benefit of victory.

sentences.zh: 就如所料，其利猶未可必然。

translations.literal: Even if it goes as they calculate, the benefit still cannot be taken as certain.
translations.idiomatic: Even if events unfold as they predict, the benefit is still far from certain.

sentences.zh: 彼江之南其地尚廣，雖無淮南豈不能集數萬之眾，伺我有警而出師耶。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi their territory is still broad; even without Huainan, can they not gather tens of thousands, watch for our alarm, and march out?
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi their territory remains vast. Even without Huainan, can they not raise tens of thousands of men and march out when they see us distracted?

sentences.zh: 戰而勝且如此，如不勝害將若何。

translations.literal: If victorious in battle it is still thus; if not victorious, what will the harm be like?
translations.idiomatic: If victory still brings such risks, what harm awaits us if we lose?

sentences.zh: 且我以騎當彼之步，理宜萬全，臣猶恐其有不敢恃者。

translations.literal: Moreover, we with cavalry against their infantry—by principle it ought to be utterly secure—yet your servant still fears there may be what cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: We would meet their infantry with our cavalry, which in principle should make victory certain, yet I still fear there may be grounds we cannot rely on.

sentences.zh: 蓋今之事勢與泰和不同。

translations.literal: For today's situation and momentum differ from Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Today's circumstances differ from those of the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 泰和以冬征，今我以夏往，此天時之不同也。

translations.literal: Taihe campaigned in winter; now we go in summer—this is the difference of Heaven's seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe campaigned in winter; we would go in summer. That is one difference in season.

sentences.zh: 冬則水涸而陸多，夏則水潦而塗淖，此地利之不同也。

translations.literal: In winter waters dry and land is plentiful; in summer waters flood and mud is deep—this is the difference of Earth's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: In winter the rivers run low and dry land is plentiful; in summer the waters rise and the roads turn to mud. That is a difference in terrain.

sentences.zh: 泰和舉天下全力，驅颭軍以為前鋒，今能之乎？

translations.literal: Taihe mustered the full strength of the realm and drove the Fengyang army as vanguard—can we do that now?
translations.idiomatic: Taihe mobilized the full strength of the realm and drove the Fengyang army as vanguard. Can we do that today?

sentences.zh: 此人事之不同也。

translations.literal: This is the difference of human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That is a difference in human resources.

sentences.zh: 議者徒見泰和之易，而不知今日之難。

translations.literal: Deliberators only see the ease of Taihe and do not know today's difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Those who debate the matter see only how easy Taihe was and do not understand how hard today would be.

sentences.zh: 請以夏人觀之，向日弓箭手之在西邊者，一遇敵則搏而戰、袒而射，彼已奔北之不暇，今乃陷吾城而虜守臣，敗吾軍而禽主將。

translations.literal: Please observe it from the Xia people: formerly the bowmen on the western border, once they met the enemy, grappled and fought and bared their arms to shoot; the enemy had no leisure but to flee north. Now they capture our cities and take our defending officials prisoner, defeat our armies and capture our commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Western Xia. Once our bowmen on the western frontier grappled and fought bare-armed at the first contact, and the enemy had no time but to flee. Now they take our cities and capture our defending officials, defeat our armies and seize our commanders.

sentences.zh: 曩則畏我如彼，今則侮我如此。

translations.literal: Formerly they feared us as that; now they insult us as this.
translations.idiomatic: They once feared us as they did then; now they treat us with contempt.

sentences.zh: 夫以夏人既非前日，奈何以宋人獨如前日哉。

translations.literal: Since the Xia people are already not as in former days, how can the Song alone be as in former days?
translations.idiomatic: If the Xia are no longer what they once were, how can we assume the Song alone remain unchanged?

sentences.zh: 願陛下思其勝之之利，又思敗之之害，無悅甘言，無貽後悔。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would think of the benefit of victory and also think of the harm of defeat, not delight in sweet words, and not bequeath regret.'
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to weigh the gains of victory and the harm of defeat, not to delight in flattering words, and not to leave yourself regret.'

sentences.zh: 章奏不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was not answered.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 時全果大敗於淮上，一軍全沒。

translations.literal: Shi Quan was indeed greatly defeated on the Huai; one whole army was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Quan was indeed routed on the Huai, and an entire army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 宣宗責諸將曰：「當使我何面目見楊雲翼耶？」

translations.literal: Xuanzong reproached the generals: 'What face should I have to meet Yang Yunyi?'
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong rebuked the generals: 'What face can I show Yang Yunyi now?'

sentences.zh: 河朔民十有一人為遊騎所迫，泅河而南，有司論罪當死，雲翼曰：「法所重私渡者，防奸偽也。

translations.literal: Eleven out of ten commoners of Heshuo, pressed by roaming cavalry, swam the river southward. The offices judged the crime deserving death. Yunyi said: 'What the law weighs heavily in private crossing is to guard against treachery and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: In Heshuo, nine out of ten civilians forced by enemy scouts to swim the river south were sentenced to death. Yunyi said: 'The law punishes unauthorized river crossings to prevent spies and traitors.

sentences.zh: 今平民為兵所迫，奔入於河，為逭死之計耳。

translations.literal: Now commoners are pressed by soldiers, rush into the river—it is only a plan to escape death.
translations.idiomatic: These were ordinary people driven by enemy troops into the river simply to escape death.

sentences.zh: 今使不死於敵而死於法，後惟從敵而已。」

translations.literal: If now they do not die at the enemy's hands but die by the law, afterward they will follow only the enemy.'
translations.idiomatic: If they die not by the enemy's hand but by our law, hereafter they will have no choice but to join the enemy.'

sentences.zh: 宣宗悟，盡釋之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong understood and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong understood and released them all.

sentences.zh: 哀宗以河南旱，詔遣官理冤獄，而不及陝西，雲翼言：「天地人通為一體，今人一支受病則四體為之不寧，豈可專治受病之處而置其餘哉。」

translations.literal: Aizong, because Henan suffered drought, issued an edict sending officials to settle wrongful cases, but it did not reach Shaanxi. Yunyi said: 'Heaven, Earth, and Man pass through as one body; if today one limb is ill, the four limbs are thereby unquiet—how can one treat only the place that is ill and set aside the rest?'
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck Henan, Aizong ordered officials to review wrongful convictions there but not in Shaanxi. Yunyi said: 'Heaven, earth, and humanity form one body. When one limb falls ill, the whole body suffers. How can we treat only the afflicted part and ignore the rest?'

sentences.zh: 朝廷是之。

translations.literal: The court approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 司天有以《太乙新曆》上進者，尚書省檄雲翼參訂，摘其不合者二十餘條，曆家稱焉。

translations.literal: Someone in the Directorate of Astronomy presented the New Taoyi Calendar upward; the Secretariat dispatched Yunyi to revise it jointly. He picked out more than twenty items that did not conform, and calendar experts praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Directorate of Astronomy submitted the New Taoyi Calendar, the Secretariat ordered Yunyi to review it. He identified more than twenty errors, and the calendar specialists praised his work.

sentences.zh: 所著文集若干卷，校《大金禮儀》若干卷，《續通鑑》若干卷，《周禮辨》一篇，《左氏》、《莊》、《列賦》各一篇，《五星聚井辨》一篇，《縣象賦》一篇，《勾股機要》、《象數雜說》等著藏於家。

translations.literal: His collected writings number several juan; he collated several juan of the Rites of the Great Jin; several juan of Continued Comprehensive Mirror; one piece on the Rites of Zhou; one rhapsody each on the Zuo Tradition, Zhuangzi, and Liezi; one piece on the Five Stars Gathering at the Well; one rhapsody on the Suspended Images; Essential Methods of Gougu and Miscellaneous Discourses on Numbers and Images—these works and others are stored in his house.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in several volumes, collated several volumes of the Rites of the Great Jin, compiled several volumes of a Continued Comprehensive Mirror, and wrote such works as Discourse on the Rites of Zhou, rhapsodies on the Zuo Tradition, Zhuangzi, and Liezi, Discourse on the Five Stars Gathering at the Well, Rhapsody on the Suspended Images, Essential Methods of Gougu, and Miscellaneous Discourses on Numbers and Images, all kept in his household.

sentences.zh: 趙秉文

translations.literal: Zhao Bingwen
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bingwen

sentences.zh: 趙秉文，字周臣，磁州滏陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Bingwen, styled Zhouchen, was a man of Fuyang in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bingwen, whose style name was Zhouchen, came from Fuyang in Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，讀書若夙習。

translations.literal: In youth he was perceptive; in reading books it was as if long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was exceptionally bright and took to books as though he had studied them from birth.

sentences.zh: 登大定二十五年進士第，調安塞簿，以課最遷邯鄲令，再遷唐山。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-fifth year of Dading, was assigned as recorder of Anse, and for top performance in duties was moved to magistrate of Handan, then again to Tangshan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Dading, was appointed clerk of Anse, and for outstanding performance was promoted to magistrate of Handan and then of Tangshan.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，用薦者起複南京路轉運司都勾判官。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; on recommendation he was recalled to serve as Chief Intendant Clerk of the Nanjing Circuit Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he left office for mourning, then on recommendation was recalled to serve as Chief Intendant Clerk on the Nanjing Circuit Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 明昌六年，入為應奉翰林文字，同知制誥。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Mingchang he entered the capital as Hanlin Attendant for Documentation, concurrently Associate Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Mingchang he entered the capital as Hanlin Attendant for Documentation and Associate Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 上書論宰相胥持國當罷，宗室守貞可大用。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial arguing that Chancellor Xu Chiguo ought to be dismissed and the imperial clansman Shouzhen could be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial arguing that Chancellor Xu Chiguo should be dismissed and that the imperial clansman Shouzhen deserved greater employment.

sentences.zh: 章宗召問，言頗差異，於是命知大興府事內族膏等鞫之。

translations.literal: Zhangzong summoned him for questioning; his words differed considerably, and he thereupon ordered the Administrator of Daxing Prefecture, the imperial clansman Gao, and others to try him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong summoned him for questioning. His account differed markedly from expectation, so the emperor ordered the Administrator of Daxing Prefecture, the imperial clansman Gao, and others to investigate.

sentences.zh: 秉文初不肯言，詰其僕，歷數交遊者，秉文乃曰：「初欲上言，嘗與修撰王庭筠、御史周昂、省令史潘豹、鄭贊道、高坦等私議。」

translations.literal: Bingwen at first refused to speak; they questioned his servant, who listed his associates one by one. Bingwen then said: 'When I first wished to submit the memorial, I once privately discussed it with Compiler Wang Tingjian, Censor Zhou Ang, Secretariat Clerk Pan Bao, Zheng Zandao, Gao Tan, and others.'
translations.idiomatic: At first Bingwen refused to speak. They questioned his servant, who named his associates one by one. Bingwen then said: 'When I first planned to submit the memorial, I had privately discussed it with Compiler Wang Tingjian, Censor Zhou Ang, Secretariat Clerk Pan Bao, Zheng Zandao, Gao Tan, and others.'

sentences.zh: 庭筠等皆下獄，決罰有差。

translations.literal: Tingjian and the others were all put in prison; punishments were decided with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Tingjian and the others were all imprisoned and punished to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 有司論秉文上書狂妄，法當追解，上不欲以言罪人，遂特免焉。

translations.literal: The offices judged that Bingwen's memorial was reckless and by law he ought to be dismissed and pursued; the emperor did not wish to make men guilty for words and specially exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities ruled that Bingwen's memorial was reckless and that by law he should be dismissed. The emperor did not wish to punish a man for his words and specially exempted him.

sentences.zh: 當時為之語曰：「古有硃雲，今有秉文，硃雲攀檻，秉文攀人。」

translations.literal: At the time people made a saying of it: 'In antiquity there was Zhu Yun; today there is Bingwen. Zhu Yun grasped the balustrade; Bingwen grasped men.'
translations.idiomatic: People at the time said: 'In antiquity there was Zhu Yun; today there is Bingwen. Zhu Yun seized the balustrade; Bingwen seized men.'

sentences.zh: 士大夫莫不恥之。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials were all ashamed of it.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials were unanimous in their shame.

sentences.zh: 坐是久廢，後起為同知岢嵐軍州事，轉北京路轉運司支度判官。

translations.literal: Because of this he was long idle; later he was raised as Associate Administrator of Keilan Military Prefecture, then transferred to Expenditure Judicial Officer of the Beijing Circuit Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he remained out of office for a long time. Later he was appointed Associate Administrator of Keilan Military Prefecture, then transferred to Expenditure Judicial Officer on the Beijing Circuit Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 承安五年冬十月，陰晦連日，宰相張萬公入對，上顧謂萬公曰：「卿言天日晦冥，亦猶人君用人邪正不分，極有理。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the fifth year of Chengan, gloom continued for days on end. Chancellor Zhang Wangong entered for audience. The emperor turned and said to Wangong: 'What you said—that heaven and sun are dim and dark—is also like a ruler employing men without distinguishing the upright from the depraved. It is extremely reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the fifth year of Chengan, the sky stayed dark for days on end. When Chancellor Zhang Wangong came to audience, the emperor turned to him and said: 'What you said about heaven and sun growing dim is much like a ruler who cannot tell the upright from the wicked in his appointments. That is very well put.

sentences.zh: 若趙秉文曩以言事降授，聞其人有才藻，工書翰，又且敢言，朕非棄不用，以北邊軍事方興，姑試之耳。」

translations.literal: As for Zhao Bingwen, who was formerly demoted for memorializing on affairs—I have heard the man has literary talent, is skilled in calligraphy, and moreover dares to speak. We have not cast him aside unused; with northern border military affairs just rising, We are merely testing him for now.'
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhao Bingwen, who was once demoted for speaking out on state affairs, I have heard he has literary talent, excels at calligraphy, and dares to speak frankly. I have not cast him aside. With military affairs on the northern frontier just heating up, I am merely testing him for now.'

sentences.zh: 泰和二年，召為戶部主事，遷翰林修撰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Revenue, then moved to Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Revenue and then promoted to Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 十月，出為甯邊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he went out as Prefect of Ningbian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was posted as Prefect of Ningbian.

sentences.zh: 三年，改平定州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to Pingding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Pingding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 前政苛于用刑，每聞赦將至，先掊賊死乃拜赦，而盜愈繁。

translations.literal: The previous administration was harsh in applying punishments; whenever they heard an amnesty was coming, they first beat thieves to death and only then accepted the amnesty, yet banditry grew ever more frequent.
translations.idiomatic: The previous administration was harsh in applying punishments. Whenever word came that an amnesty was near, officials would beat thieves to death first and only then accept the amnesty, yet banditry only grew worse.

sentences.zh: 秉文為政，一從寬簡，旬月盜悉屏跡。

translations.literal: Bingwen in governing followed leniency and simplicity throughout; within a month and ten days bandits all vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen governed with leniency and simplicity, and within a month bandits had all vanished.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，出祿粟倡豪民以賑，全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he distributed his salary grain and urged wealthy households to relieve the people; those fully saved were very many.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he distributed his salary grain and urged wealthy households to join the relief effort, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 大安初，北兵南向，召秉文與待制趙資道論備邊策，秉文言：「今我軍聚於宣德，城小，列營其外，涉暑雨，器械弛敗，人且病，俟秋敵至將不利矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daan, northern troops marched south. Bingwen was summoned with Attendant-in-Waiting Zhao Zidao to discuss border defense strategy. Bingwen said: 'Now our army is gathered at Xuande; the city is small and camps are arrayed outside it. Exposed to summer heat and rain, weapons slacken and break, and men are falling ill. When the enemy arrives in autumn it will be unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daan, as northern troops marched south, Bingwen was summoned with Attendant-in-Waiting Zhao Zidao to discuss border defense. Bingwen said: 'Our army is now massed at Xuande. The city is small and the camps lie outside its walls. Exposed to summer heat and rain, weapons are failing and men are falling ill. When the enemy arrives in autumn, we will be at a grave disadvantage.

sentences.zh: 可遣臨潢一軍搗其虛，則山西之圍可解，兵法所謂'出其不意、攻其必救'者也。」

translations.literal: We may dispatch an army from Linhuang to strike their empty point; then the encirclement of Shanxi can be relieved. This is what military strategy calls "strike where they do not expect it; attack what they must rescue."'
translations.idiomatic: We could send an army from Linhuang to strike where they are weak, and the encirclement of Shanxi would be lifted. That is what military strategy calls striking where the enemy does not expect it and attacking what he must rescue.'

sentences.zh: 衛王不能用，其秋宣德果以敗聞。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei could not employ it; that autumn defeat at Xuande was indeed reported.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei would not adopt his advice, and that autumn news came of defeat at Xuande.

sentences.zh: 尋為兵部郎中，兼翰林修撰，俄轉翰林直學士。

translations.literal: Shortly he became Director in the Ministry of War, concurrently Hanlin Compiler, and soon was moved to Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Director in the Ministry of War and Hanlin Compiler, then shortly promoted to Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，建言時事可行者三：一遷都，二導河，三封建。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he offered counsel on three timely measures that could be carried out: relocating the capital, channeling the river, and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenyou he proposed three timely measures: relocating the capital, channeling the Yellow River, and restoring enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 朝廷略施行之。

translations.literal: The court broadly carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted them in part.

sentences.zh: 明年，上書願為國家守殘破一州，以宣佈朝廷恤民之意，且曰：「陛下勿謂書生不知兵，顏真卿、張巡、許遠輩以身許國，亦書生也。」

translations.literal: The next year he submitted a memorial wishing to hold one broken remnant prefecture for the state, to proclaim the court's care for the people, and said: 'Your Majesty must not think that scholar-officials do not know warfare. Yan Zhenqing, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, and their kind devoted their persons to the state—they too were scholar-officials.'
translations.idiomatic: The following year he submitted a memorial offering to hold one battered prefecture for the state so as to proclaim the court's care for the people. He said: 'Your Majesty must not assume that scholars know nothing of war. Yan Zhenqing, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, and men like them gave their lives to the state, and they were scholars too.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「使臣死而有益於國，猶勝坐糜廩祿為無用之人。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'If your servant dies yet it benefits the state, it is still better than sitting and consuming granary salary as a useless man.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'If my death should benefit the state, that is still better than sitting idle on court salary as a useless man.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「秉文志固可尚，然方今翰苑尤難其人，卿宿儒，當在左右。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Bingwen's resolve is indeed admirable, yet at present the Hanlin Academy especially lacks such a man. You are a veteran scholar and ought to remain at Our side.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Bingwen's resolve is admirable, but the Hanlin Academy especially needs such a man just now. You are a veteran scholar and should remain at my side.'

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: He did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜翰林侍講學士，言：「寶券滯塞，蓋朝廷初議更張，市肆已妄傳其不用，因之抑遏，漸至廢絕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Hanlin Attendant Lecturer and said: 'Treasury notes are stagnant and blocked. It is because when the court first deliberated on reform, the markets already falsely spread word that they would not be used; because of this they were suppressed and gradually came to abandonment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Hanlin Attendant Lecturer and said: 'Treasury notes have ceased to circulate. When the court first debated reform, the markets falsely spread word that the notes would be abolished. They were suppressed and have gradually fallen out of use altogether.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜立回易務，令近上職官通市道者掌之，給以銀鈔粟麥縑帛之類，權其低昂而出納。」

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks we ought to establish an Exchange Office, order high-ranking officials who understand markets to administer it, supply it with silver notes, grain, wheat, silk, cloth, and the like, weigh their rise and fall, and issue and receive them.'
translations.idiomatic: I believe we should establish an Exchange Office run by senior officials who understand commerce, stocked with silver notes, grain, wheat, silk, and cloth, and regulate prices as goods are issued and received.'

sentences.zh: 詔有司議行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate and carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate and implement the plan.

sentences.zh: 五年，複為禮部尚書，入謝，上曰：「卿春秋高，以文章故須複用卿。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again became Minister of Rites. Entering to give thanks, the emperor said: 'You are advanced in years; because of your writings We must again employ you.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was again appointed Minister of Rites. When he came to give thanks, the emperor said: 'You are advanced in years, but because of your writings I must put you back in office.'

sentences.zh: 秉文以身受厚恩，無以自效，願開忠言、廣聖慮，每進見從容為上言，人主當儉勤、慎兵刑，所以祈天永命者，上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: Bingwen, having received thick favor in person and having no means to repay it himself, wished to open loyal words and broaden the sage's deliberation. Each time he entered audience he calmly spoke to the emperor that the ruler ought to be frugal and diligent and cautious in warfare and punishments—the means by which one prays Heaven for enduring mandate—and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen, having received such great favor and unable to repay it adequately, sought to offer loyal counsel and broaden the emperor's vision. Whenever he attended audience he calmly urged that a ruler should be frugal, diligent, and cautious in war and punishments—the means by which one prays Heaven for a lasting mandate—and the emperor approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 哀宗即位，再乞致仕，不許。

translations.literal: When Aizong took the throne he twice begged to retire; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Aizong ascended the throne, Bingwen twice asked to retire, but both requests were denied.

sentences.zh: 改翰林學士，同修國史，兼益政院說書官。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hanlin Academician, concurrently Compiler of the National History, and Lecturer at the Bureau for Promoting Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin Academician, Compiler of the National History, and Lecturer at the Bureau for Promoting Governance.

sentences.zh: 以上嗣德在初，當日親經史以自裨益，進《無逸直解》、《貞觀政要》、《申鑒》各一通。

translations.literal: Because the heir's virtue was at its beginning, he ought daily to attend to the classics and histories for his own benefit. He presented one copy each of Direct Explication of "Against Idleness," Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign, and Shen Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Because the heir's character was still being formed, he ought daily to study the classics and histories for his own improvement. Bingwen presented one copy each of Direct Explication of "Against Idleness," Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign, and Shen Jian.

sentences.zh: 正大九年正月，汴京戒嚴，上命秉文為赦文，以布宣悔悟哀痛之意。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Zhengda, Bianjing was placed under martial law. The emperor ordered Bingwen to draft the amnesty edict, to proclaim repentance, awakening, and grief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year of Zhengda, Bianjing was placed under martial law. The emperor ordered Bingwen to draft the amnesty edict expressing repentance and grief.

sentences.zh: 秉文指事陳義，辭情俱盡。

translations.literal: Bingwen pointed to affairs and set forth principles; in wording and feeling both were fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen cited concrete events and laid out their moral meaning with complete force of language and feeling.

sentences.zh: 及兵退，大臣欲稱賀，且命為表，秉文曰：「《春秋》'新宮火，三日哭'。

translations.literal: When the troops withdrew, great ministers wished to offer congratulations and also ordered him to draft a congratulatory memorial. Bingwen said: 'In the Spring and Autumn Annals, "When the new palace caught fire, there was mourning for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, senior ministers wished to offer congratulations and ordered him to draft a congratulatory memorial. Bingwen said: 'The Spring and Autumn Annals records that when the new palace caught fire, there was mourning for three days.

sentences.zh: 今園陵如此，酌之以禮，當慰不當賀。」

translations.literal: Now the imperial tombs are in such a state; measured by ritual, one ought to offer consolation, not congratulations.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial tombs lie in such a state. Judged by ritual propriety, we ought to offer consolation, not congratulations.'

sentences.zh: 遂已。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時年已老，日以時事為憂，雖食息頃不能忘。

translations.literal: By then he was already old and daily took current affairs as his worry; even in the moments of eating and breathing he could not forget.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was old and worried constantly about current affairs, unable to forget them even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 每聞一事可便民，一士可擢用，大則拜章，小則為當路者言，殷勤鄭重，不能自已。

translations.literal: Whenever he heard of one matter that could benefit the people or one gentleman who could be promoted and employed, for great matters he submitted a memorial, for small ones he spoke to those in power—earnest and grave, unable to restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he heard of some measure that could benefit the people or some worthy man who deserved promotion, he would memorialize on great matters and speak privately to those in power on lesser ones, earnest and insistent, unable to restrain himself.

sentences.zh: 三月，草《開興改元詔》，閭巷間皆能傳誦，洛陽人拜詔畢，舉城痛哭，其感人如此。

translations.literal: In the third month he drafted the Edict on Opening Prosperity and Changing the Reign Era. In lanes and alleys all could recite and chant it. When the people of Luoyang finished bowing to the edict, the whole city wept together—such was its power to move men.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he drafted the Edict on Opening Prosperity and Changing the Reign Era. People in every lane could recite it from memory. When the people of Luoyang finished bowing to the edict, the whole city wept together. Such was its power to move them.

sentences.zh: 是年五月壬辰，卒，年七十四，積官至資善大夫、上護軍、天水郡侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year, on the day renchen, he died, aged seventy-four. Through accumulated offices he reached Worthy and Good Grand Master, Upper Guardian of the Army, and Marquis of the Tianshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year, on the day renchen, he died at the age of seventy-four, having risen through accumulated offices to Worthy and Good Grand Master, Upper Guardian of the Army, and Marquis of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 正大間，同楊雲翼作《龜鑑萬年錄》上之。

translations.literal: During Zhengda, together with Yang Yunyi he composed Records of the Tortoise Mirror for Ten Thousand Years and presented it upward.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengda era he collaborated with Yang Yunyi on Records of the Tortoise Mirror for Ten Thousand Years and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又因進講，與雲翼共集自古治術，號《君臣政要》為一編以進焉。

translations.literal: Also, taking advantage of advancing to lecture, together with Yunyi he collected governing methods from antiquity, titled Essential Policies of Ruler and Minister as one compilation, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while lecturing at court, he and Yunyi compiled governing methods from antiquity into a work titled Essential Policies of Ruler and Minister and presented it.

sentences.zh: 秉文自幼至老未嘗一日廢書，著《易叢說》十卷，《中庸說》一卷，《揚子發微》一卷，《太玄箋贊》六卷，《文中子類說》一卷，《南華略釋》一卷，《列子補注》一卷，刪集《論語》、《孟子解》各一十卷，《資暇錄》一十五卷，所著文章號《滏水集》者三十卷。

translations.literal: From youth to old age Bingwen never for one day abandoned books. He authored Collected Discourses on the Changes in ten juan, Discourse on the Mean in one juan, Unfolding the Subtle in the Yangzi in one juan, Annotated Praise of the Supreme Mystery in six juan, Classified Sayings of Wenzhongzi in one juan, Brief Explication of the Zhuangzi in one juan, Supplementary Notes on the Liezi in one juan, abridged and collected Explications of the Analects and Mencius in ten juan each, Records of Leisure Learning in fifteen juan, and his collected writings titled Fu River Collection in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age Bingwen never went a day without reading. His works included Collected Discourses on the Changes in ten volumes, Discourse on the Mean in one volume, Unfolding the Subtle in the Yangzi in one volume, Annotated Praise of the Supreme Mystery in six volumes, Classified Sayings of Wenzhongzi in one volume, Brief Explication of the Zhuangzi in one volume, Supplementary Notes on the Liezi in one volume, abridged editions of Explications of the Analects and Mencius in ten volumes each, Records of Leisure Learning in fifteen volumes, and his collected writings, the Fu River Collection, in thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 秉文之文長於辨析，極所欲言而止，不以繩墨自拘。

translations.literal: Bingwen's writings excel in analysis and discrimination; he stops when he has fully said what he wishes and does not constrain himself with rules and measures.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen's prose excelled in clear analysis. He said what he had to say and stopped, never binding himself to formal rules.

sentences.zh: 七言長詩筆勢縱放，不拘一律，律詩壯麗，小詩精絕，多以近體為之，至五言古詩則沉鬱頓挫。

translations.literal: His seven-character long poems wield the brush with free abandon and are not bound to one pattern; regulated verse is magnificent, short poems are consummate. He mostly used recent forms, while in five-character ancient verse he is somber, weighty, and forcefully restrained.
translations.idiomatic: His long seven-character poems were bold and unrestrained, never bound to one pattern. His regulated verse was magnificent and his short poems exquisite, mostly in recent forms, while his five-character ancient verse was somber and forceful.

sentences.zh: 字畫則草書尤遒勁。

translations.literal: In calligraphy his cursive script is especially powerful and vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: In calligraphy his cursive script was especially powerful.

sentences.zh: 朝使至自河、湟者，多言夏人問秉文及王庭筠起居狀，其為四方所重如此。

translations.literal: Court envoys coming from the He and Huang regions often said the Xia people inquired after Bingwen's and Wang Tingjian's health and circumstances—such was the weight he carried in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Court envoys returning from the He and Huang regions often reported that the Western Xia inquired after the health of Bingwen and Wang Tingjian. Such was the esteem in which he was held across the realm.

sentences.zh: 為人至誠樂易，與人交不立崖岸，未嘗以大名自居。

translations.literal: As a man he was utterly sincere, cheerful, and easy; in dealing with others he did not set up steep banks and cliffs, and never took his great name upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was utterly sincere, cheerful, and approachable. In friendship he set up no barriers and never traded on his great reputation.

sentences.zh: 仕五朝，官六卿，自奉養如寒士。

translations.literal: He served five reigns and held office among the six ministries, yet supported himself like a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He served five reigns and rose to the six ministries, yet lived as simply as a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 楊雲翼嘗與秉文代掌文柄，時人號「楊趙」。

translations.literal: Yang Yunyi once with Bingwen alternately held the literary brush; people of the time called them "Yang and Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunyi and Bingwen once alternately held literary authority at court, and contemporaries called them "Yang and Zhao."

sentences.zh: 然晚年頗以禪語自汙，人亦以為秉文之恨雲。

translations.literal: Yet in his later years he rather defiled himself with Chan phrases, and people also took this as a cloud of regret over Bingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his later years he rather sullied himself with Chan Buddhist language, which people took as a stain on Bingwen's reputation.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：楊雲翼、趙秉文，金士巨擘，其文墨論議以及政事皆有足傳。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yang Yunyi and Zhao Bingwen were great pillars among Jin scholars; their writings, deliberations, and governmental affairs all have sufficient worth to be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Yang Yunyi and Zhao Bingwen were towering figures among Jin scholars. Their writings, counsel, and public service all deserve to be remembered.

sentences.zh: 雲翼諫伐宋一疏，宣宗雖不見聽，此心何愧景略。

translations.literal: Yunyi's one memorial remonstrating against campaigning against Song—though Xuanzong did not heed it, what shame is there in this heart compared with Jinglue?
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi's memorial against campaigning against Song went unheeded by Xuanzong, yet what shame does his conscience owe to Wang Meng?

sentences.zh: 庭筠之累，秉文所為，茲事大愧高允。

translations.literal: The trouble that fell on Tingjian was Bingwen's doing; in this matter there is great shame compared with Gao Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble that fell on Tingjian was Bingwen's doing, and in this matter he falls far short of Gao Yun.

sentences.zh: 韓玉，字溫甫，其先相人，曾祖錫仕金，以濟南尹致仕。

translations.literal: Han Yu, styled Wenfu, his ancestors were men of Xiang. His great-grandfather Xi served the Jin and retired as Administrator of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, whose style name was Wenfu, came from Xiang. His great-grandfather Xi served the Jin and retired as Administrator of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 玉明昌五年經義、辭賦兩科進士，入翰林為應奉。

translations.literal: Yu in the fifth year of Mingchang passed both the jingyi and cifu examinations as jinshi and entered the Hanlin as Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yu passed both the jingyi and cifu examinations as jinshi in the fifth year of Mingchang and entered the Hanlin as an Attendant.

sentences.zh: 應制一日百篇，文不加點。

translations.literal: On imperial command he wrote a hundred pieces in one day, the text needing no punctuation.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial command he wrote a hundred pieces in a single day without needing to revise a stroke.

sentences.zh: 又作《元勳傳》，稱旨，章宗歎曰：「勳臣何幸，得此家作傳耶！」

translations.literal: He also composed Biographies of Founding Merit, which met with approval. Zhangzong sighed and said: 'How fortunate are the meritorious ministers to have this household write their biographies!'
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Biographies of Founding Merit, which pleased the emperor. Zhangzong sighed and said: 'How fortunate are our meritorious ministers to have this family write their biographies!'

sentences.zh: 泰和中，建言開通州潞水漕渠，船運至都。

translations.literal: During Taihe he offered counsel to open the Tongzhou Lushui transport canal so that shipping reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he proposed opening the Tongzhou Lushui transport canal so that grain could be shipped to the capital by boat.

sentences.zh: 升兩階，授同知陝西東路轉運使事。

translations.literal: He was raised two ranks and appointed Associate Commissioner of the Shaanxi Eastern Circuit Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted two ranks and appointed Associate Commissioner of the Shaanxi Eastern Circuit Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，都城受圍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daan the capital was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daan the capital came under siege.

sentences.zh: 夏人連陷邠、涇，陝西安撫司檄玉以鳳翔總管判官為都統府募軍，旬日得萬人，與夏人戰，敗之，獲牛馬千餘。

translations.literal: The Xia people in succession captured Bin and Jing. The Shaanxi Pacification Commission dispatched Yu, as judicial officer to the Fengxiang Commander-in-Chief, to recruit troops for the General Command. Within ten days he obtained ten thousand men, fought the Xia, defeated them, and captured more than a thousand cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Xia overran Bin and Jing in succession. The Shaanxi Pacification Commission ordered Yu, serving as judicial officer under the Fengxiang Commander-in-Chief, to recruit troops for the General Command. Within ten days he raised ten thousand men, defeated the Xia in battle, and captured more than a thousand cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 時夏兵五萬方圍平涼，又戰于北原，夏人疑大軍至，是夜解去。

translations.literal: At that time fifty thousand Xia troops were besieging Pingliang. He fought again at Beiyuan; the Xia suspected a great army had arrived and that night lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time fifty thousand Xia troops were besieging Pingliang. He fought again at Beiyuan, and the Xia, suspecting that a large army had arrived, lifted the siege that night and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 當路者忌其功，驛奏玉與夏寇有謀，朝廷疑之，使使者授玉河平軍節度副使，且覘其軍。

translations.literal: Those in power envied his merit and reported by post that Yu had plotted with the Xia bandits. The court suspected him and sent an envoy to appoint Yu Vice Military Commissioner of Heping Army while also observing his army.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power envied his success and reported by courier that Yu had plotted with the Xia. The court grew suspicious and sent an envoy to appoint him Vice Military Commissioner of the Heping Army while also observing his troops.

sentences.zh: 先是，華州李公直以都城隔絕，謀舉兵入援，而玉恃其軍為可用，亦欲為勤王之舉，乃傳檄州郡雲：「事推其本，禍有所基，始自賊臣貪容奸賂，繼緣二帥貪固威權。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Gongzhi of Huazhou, because the capital was cut off, plotted to raise troops to enter and relieve it. Yu, relying on his army as usable, also wished to make a loyalist rescue and thereupon circulated a proclamation to prefectures and commanderies saying: 'Affairs trace back to their root; calamity has its foundation. It began with wicked ministers who greedily harbored treachery and bribes, and continued through two commanders who greedily clung to power and authority.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Gongzhi of Huazhou, finding the capital cut off, plotted to raise troops to relieve it. Yu, trusting that his army could be used, also wished to march to the emperor's aid and circulated a proclamation to the prefectures saying: 'Affairs trace back to their root, and calamity has its foundation. It began with wicked ministers who greedily harbored treachery and bribes, and continued through two commanders who greedily clung to power.'

sentences.zh: 又雲：「裹糧坐費，盡膏血於生民。

translations.literal: It also said: 'Wrapping grain and sitting to consume it, they exhaust the lifeblood of the people.
translations.idiomatic: It also said: 'They consume rations without fighting and drain the lifeblood of the people.

sentences.zh: 棄甲複來，竭資儲于國計。

translations.literal: Casting off armor and coming back again, they exhaust the state's stores in the national accounts.
translations.idiomatic: They cast off their armor and return again, draining the state's reserves.

sentences.zh: 要權力而望形勢，連歲月而守妻孥。」

translations.literal: They demand power and watch the situation, guarding wives and children for months on end.'
translations.idiomatic: They grasp for power while watching how the wind blows, staying with their wives and children month after month.'

sentences.zh: 又雲：「人誰無死，有臣子之當然。

translations.literal: It also said: 'Who among men does not die? There is what is proper for subjects and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: It also said: 'Who among men does not die? Yet there is what is proper for a subject and minister.

sentences.zh: 事至於今，忍君親之弗顧。

translations.literal: Matters have come to today, yet they bear not to regard ruler and parent.
translations.idiomatic: Matters have come to this pass, yet they cannot bring themselves to care for ruler and kin.

sentences.zh: 而謂百年身後，虛名一聽史臣。

translations.literal: Yet they say that a hundred years after their bodies, empty fame will be left entirely to the historians.
translations.idiomatic: They think that a hundred years after death, empty fame will be left entirely to the historians.

sentences.zh: 只如今日目前，何顏以居人世。」

translations.literal: Only as for today before their eyes, what face have they to dwell in the human world?'
translations.idiomatic: As for the present moment before their eyes, what face have they to show in this world?'

sentences.zh: 公直一軍行有日矣，將有違約、國朝人有不從者，輒以軍法從事。

translations.literal: Gongzhi's army had been on the march for days. When there were those who would break the agreement or Jin subjects who would not follow, he immediately applied military law.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi's army had been on the march for days. Anyone who broke the agreement or any subject of the dynasty who refused to follow was dealt with by military law.

sentences.zh: 京兆統軍便謂公直據華州反，遣都統楊珪襲取之，遂置極刑。

translations.literal: The Jingzhao Commander-in-Chief then said Gongzhi held Huazhou in rebellion, dispatched Commander-in-Chief Yang Gui to seize him by surprise, and thereupon imposed the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhao Commander-in-Chief declared that Gongzhi had seized Huazhou in rebellion, sent Commander-in-Chief Yang Gui to take him by surprise, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 公直曾為書約玉，玉不預知，其書乃為安撫所得。

translations.literal: Gongzhi had once written a letter making an agreement with Yu; Yu did not know beforehand, and the letter was obtained by the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi had once written Yu a letter proposing joint action. Yu had not known of it beforehand, and the letter fell into the hands of the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 及使者覘玉軍，且疑預公直之謀，即實其罪。

translations.literal: When the envoy observed Yu's army and also suspected he had foreknown Gongzhi's plot, he immediately confirmed his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy observed Yu's army and suspected he had shared in Gongzhi's plot, he confirmed the charge against him.

sentences.zh: 玉道出華州，被囚，死於郡學。

translations.literal: Yu, on the road passing through Huazhou, was imprisoned and died in the prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, passing through Huazhou on the road, was imprisoned and died in the prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 臨終書二詩壁間，士論冤之。

translations.literal: At the end he wrote two poems on the wall; scholar opinion held him wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he wrote two poems on the wall, and scholars widely regarded his case as a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 子不疑，字居之。

translations.literal: His son Bu Yi, styled Juzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bu Yi, whose style name was Juzhi.

sentences.zh: 以父死非罪，誓不祿仕。

translations.literal: Because his father died though guilty of no crime, he swore never to take salary or office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died though guilty of no crime, he swore never to accept office or salary.

sentences.zh: 藏其父臨終時手書雲：「此去冥路，吾心皓然，剛直之氣，必不下沉。

translations.literal: He kept his father's handwritten words at the end of life, which said: 'On this road to the dark realm, my heart is bright and clear; the qi of firm uprightness will surely not sink down.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his father's last handwritten words, which read: 'On this road to the dark realm my heart remains bright and clear. The spirit of firm uprightness will surely not sink down.

sentences.zh: 兒可無慮。

translations.literal: Son, you need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Son, you need not worry.

sentences.zh: 世亂時艱，努力自護，幽明雖異，寧不見爾。」

translations.literal: The age is chaotic and times are hard; strive to protect yourself. Though dark and bright are different, how could I not see you?'
translations.idiomatic: The age is chaotic and times are hard, so strive to protect yourself. Though the living and the dead are apart, surely I shall still see you.'

sentences.zh: 讀者惻然。

translations.literal: Readers were deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: Readers were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 馮璧，字叔獻，真定縣人。

translations.literal: Feng Bi, styled Shuxian, was a man of Zhending County.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bi, whose style name was Shuxian, came from Zhending County.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟不凡，弱冠補太學生。

translations.literal: In youth he was perceptive and not ordinary; at the capping age he was selected as an Imperial Academy student.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was exceptionally bright, and at his capping age he was selected as an Imperial Academy student.

sentences.zh: 承安二年經義進士，制策複優等，調莒州軍事判官，宰相奏留校秘書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengan he passed the jingyi jinshi examination; in the policy examination he again received superior grade. He was assigned as Military Judicial Officer of Juzhou; the chancellor memorialized to retain him at the school secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chengan he passed the jingyi jinshi examination and received a superior grade in the policy examination. He was assigned as Military Judicial Officer of Juzhou, but the chancellor memorialized to keep him at the school secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，調遼濱主簿。

translations.literal: Before long he was assigned as Registrar of Liaobin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted as Registrar of Liaobin.

sentences.zh: 縣有和糴粟未給價者餘十萬斛，散貯民居，以富人掌之，有腐敗則責償於民，民殊苦之。

translations.literal: The county had more than a hundred thousand hu of harmonized-purchase grain for which price had not been paid, stored scattered in commoners' houses with wealthy men in charge of it. When it rotted they held commoners liable for compensation, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The county held more than a hundred thousand hu of harmonized-purchase grain for which payment had not yet been made, stored in scattered private homes under wealthy managers. When grain spoiled, commoners were held liable, and the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 璧白漕司，即日罷之，民大悅。

translations.literal: Bi reported to the transport commission, and that very day it was abolished; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Bi reported to the transport commission, and the practice was abolished that very day to the people's great relief.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年，調鄜州錄事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was assigned as Recorder of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he was posted as Recorder of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，伐蜀，行部檄充軍前檢察，帥府以書檄委之。

translations.literal: The next year, in the campaign against Shu, the circuit inspection office dispatched him to serve as front-line inspector; the command headquarters entrusted him with documents and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, during the campaign against Shu, the circuit inspection office assigned him as front-line inspector, and the command headquarters entrusted him with official correspondence.

sentences.zh: 章宗欲招降吳曦，詔先以文告曉之，然後用兵。

translations.literal: Zhangzong wished to induce Wu Xi to surrender and issued an edict first to enlighten him with a written proclamation, and only then to use troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong wished to induce Wu Xi to surrender and ordered that he first be addressed with a written proclamation before troops were used.

sentences.zh: 蜀人守散關不下，金兵殺獲甚眾，璧言：「彼軍拒守而並禍其民，無乃與詔旨相戾乎？」

translations.literal: The Shu people held Sans Pass and would not yield. Jin troops killed and captured very many. Bi said: 'Their army resists and holds fast yet together brings calamity on its people—is this not contrary to the edict's intent?'
