translations.idiomatic: The Shu forces held Sans Pass and would not yield. Jin troops killed and captured a great many. Bi said: 'The enemy holds the pass yet we bring calamity on their people as well. Is that not contrary to the edict's intent?'

sentences.zh: 主帥憾之，以璧招兩當潰卒，璧即日率風州已降官屬淡剛、李果偕行。

translations.literal: The commander resented it and assigned Bi to recruit routed troops from Liangdang. Bi that same day led the already surrendered Fengzhou officials Dan Gang and Li Guo to go together.
translations.idiomatic: The commander resented his words and assigned Bi to recruit routed troops from Liangdang. Bi set out that same day with the surrendered Fengzhou officials Dan Gang and Li Guo.

sentences.zh: 道逢軍士所得子女金帛牛馬皆奪付剛，使歸其家，軍士則以違制決遣之。

translations.literal: On the road he met soldiers who had obtained women, children, gold, silk, cattle, and horses; he seized them all and handed them to Gang to return to their families, while the soldiers were sentenced and sent away for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met soldiers carrying captured women, children, gold, silk, cattle, and horses. He seized them all and handed them to Gang to return to their families, while the soldiers were punished and dismissed for violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 比到兩當，軍民三萬餘眾鼓舞迎勞，璧以朝旨慰遣之。

translations.literal: When he reached Liangdang, more than thirty thousand soldiers and civilians drummed and danced to welcome and comfort him. Bi, by imperial order, consoled and dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Liangdang, more than thirty thousand soldiers and civilians came out drumming and dancing to welcome him. Bi, by imperial order, consoled them and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 及還，主帥嘉其能，奏遷一官。

translations.literal: When he returned, the commander praised his ability and memorialized to move him one rank.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the commander praised his ability and memorialized for his promotion by one rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，自東阿丞召補尚書省令史，用宗室承暉薦授應奉翰林文字，兼韓王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, from Assistant Magistrate of Dong'e he was summoned to fill a post as Secretariat Clerk in the Ministry of Works; on recommendation of the imperial clansman Chenghui he was appointed Hanlin Attendant for Documentation, concurrently Secretary of the Prince of Han's household.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned from Assistant Magistrate of Dong'e to serve as a Secretariat Clerk in the Ministry of Works. On the recommendation of the imperial clansman Chenghui he was appointed Hanlin Attendant for Documentation and Secretary of the Prince of Han's household.

sentences.zh: 俄轉太學博士。

translations.literal: Shortly he was moved to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 至甯初，忽沙虎弑逆，遂去官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhi'ning, Hushahu committed regicide, and he thereupon left office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhi'ning, when Hushahu murdered the emperor, Bi left office.

sentences.zh: 宣宗南遷，璧時避兵東方，由單父渡河詣汴梁，時相奏複前職。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong moved south, Bi was then avoiding warfare in the east. From Shanfu he crossed the river and went to Bianliang; the chief minister memorialized to restore his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong moved the court south, Bi had been avoiding the fighting in the east. He crossed the river from Shanfu to Bianliang, and the chief minister memorialized to restore his former post.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，遷翰林修撰。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou he was moved to Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyou he was promoted to Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 時山東、河朔軍六十余萬口，仰給縣官，率不逞輩竄名其間。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of Shandong and Heshuo numbered more than six hundred thousand mouths, relying on government provision, and mostly unruly men slipped their names in among them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the armies of Shandong and Heshuo numbered more than six hundred thousand men on government rations, and unruly elements had mostly slipped in among them.

sentences.zh: 詔璧攝監察御史，汰逐之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Bi to act as Investigating Censor and weed them out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Bi to serve as acting Investigating Censor and weed them out.

sentences.zh: 總領撒合問冒券四百餘口，劾案以聞，詔杖殺之，故所至爭自首，減幾及於半。

translations.literal: The Chief Controller Sahewen falsely claimed more than four hundred mouths on ration tickets. Bi impeached and reported the case; an edict ordered him beaten to death. Therefore wherever he went men competed to confess, and the numbers were reduced by nearly half.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Controller Sahewen had falsely claimed more than four hundred ration tickets. Bi impeached him and reported the case, and an edict ordered Sahewen beaten to death. Wherever Bi went, men competed to confess, and the rolls were reduced by nearly half.

sentences.zh: 複進一官。

translations.literal: He was again advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 初，監察御史本溫被命汰宗室從坦軍于孟州，軍士欲謀變，本溫懼不知所為。

translations.literal: Earlier, Investigating Censor Ben Wen was ordered to weed out the army of the imperial clansman Congtan at Mengzhou. The soldiers wished to plot mutiny, and Ben Wen was afraid and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Investigating Censor Ben Wen had been ordered to weed out the army of the imperial clansman Congtan at Mengzhou. The soldiers plotted mutiny, and Ben Wen was terrified and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 尋有旨，北軍沈思忠以下四將屯衛州，餘眾果叛入太行。

translations.literal: Shortly there was an order that the four northern generals below Shen Sizhong encamp at Weizhou; the remaining masses indeed rebelled and entered the Taihang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an order came that the four northern generals under Shen Sizhong should encamp at Weizhou. The rest of the force did rebel and fled into the Taihang Mountains.

sentences.zh: 於是，密院奏以璧代本溫竟其事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Privy Council memorialized that Bi replace Ben Wen to finish the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Privy Council then memorialized that Bi replace Ben Wen to finish the task.

sentences.zh: 璧馳至衛，召四將喻以上意。

translations.literal: Bi galloped to Wei, summoned the four generals, and explained the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Bi galloped to Weizhou, summoned the four generals, and explained the court's intent.

sentences.zh: 思忠等挾叛者請還奏之，璧責以大義，將士慚服，不日就汰者三千人。

translations.literal: Sizhong and the others, taking the rebels with them, asked to return and report. Bi rebuked them with great principle; officers and soldiers were ashamed and submitted. Within days three thousand were weeded out.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong and the others brought the rebels along and asked to return and report. Bi rebuked them on principle, and the officers and soldiers submitted in shame. Within days three thousand men were weeded out.

sentences.zh: 六月，改大理丞，與台官行關中，劾奏奸髒之尤者商州防禦使宗室重福等十數人，自是權貴側目。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and, with censorial officials, toured Guanzhong. He impeached and reported more than ten of the most corrupt, including the Defender of Shangzhou, the imperial clansman Chongfu. From this the powerful and noble looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was made Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and toured Guanzhong with censorial officials. He impeached more than ten of the worst offenders, including Defender of Shangzhou, the imperial clansman Chongfu. From then on the powerful watched him with hostility.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，以宋人拒使者于淮上，遣兵南伐，詔京東總帥紇石烈牙吾塔攻盱眙，牙吾塔不從命，乃率精騎由滁州略宣化，縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xingding, because the Song rejected envoys on the Huai, troops were dispatched on a southern campaign. An edict ordered the Shandong Eastern Commander-in-Chief He Shilie Yawuta to attack Xuyi. Yawuta did not follow orders but led elite cavalry through Chuzhou to raid Xuanhua and let his troops plunder on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xingding, because Song rejected envoys on the Huai, troops were sent on a southern campaign. An edict ordered Shandong Eastern Commander-in-Chief He Shilie Yawuta to attack Xuyi. Yawuta disobeyed and led elite cavalry through Chuzhou to raid Xuanhua, letting his men plunder freely.

sentences.zh: 故兵所至原野蕭條，絕無所資，宋人堅壁不戰，乃無功而歸。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever the army went the fields were desolate and there was nothing to supply them. The Song held their walls firm and would not fight, and they returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his army went the countryside was stripped bare and there was nothing to supply them. Song held their walls and refused battle, and the campaign returned without success.

sentences.zh: 行省奏牙吾塔故違節制，詔璧佩金符鞫之。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat memorialized that Yawuta had deliberately violated command. An edict ordered Bi to wear the gold tally and try him.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat reported that Yawuta had deliberately disobeyed orders. An edict ordered Bi to wear the gold tally and investigate him.

sentences.zh: 璧馳入牙吾塔軍，奪其金符，易以他帥攝。

translations.literal: Bi galloped into Yawuta's army, seized his gold tally, and replaced him with another commander to act in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Bi galloped into Yawuta's camp, seized his gold tally, and replaced him with another commander.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔入獄，兵士嘩噪，以吾帥無罪為言，璧怒責牙吾塔曰：「元帥欲以兵抗制使耶？

translations.literal: Yawuta entered prison and the soldiers clamored, saying their commander was guiltless. Bi angrily rebuked Yawuta: 'Commander, do you wish to use troops to resist the commissioner?
translations.idiomatic: When Yawuta was imprisoned the soldiers clamored that their commander was innocent. Bi angrily rebuked him: 'Commander, do you mean to use your troops against the commissioner?

sentences.zh: 待罪之禮恐不如此，使者還奏，獄能竟乎。」

translations.literal: The ritual of awaiting punishment surely is not like this. When the envoy returns to report, can the case be concluded?'
translations.idiomatic: The proper conduct of a man awaiting judgment is surely not this. When the envoy returns to report, do you think the case can be closed?'

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔伏地請死，璧曰：「兵法，進退自專，有失機會以致覆敗者斬。」

translations.literal: Yawuta prostrated himself and begged for death. Bi said: 'In military law, advance and retreat are one's own decision; whoever loses opportunity and brings defeat is beheaded.'
translations.idiomatic: Yawuta prostrated himself and begged for death. Bi said: 'Military law holds that advance and retreat are the commander's own decision, and whoever misses his chance and brings defeat is beheaded.'

sentences.zh: 即擬以聞，時議壯之。

translations.literal: He immediately drafted the report and submitted it; opinion at the time admired his courage.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately drafted his report and submitted it, and public opinion admired his firmness.

sentences.zh: 十月，改禮部員外郎，權右司諫、治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, acting Right Remonstrance Official and Attending Imperial Scribe Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites while acting as Right Remonstrance Official and Attending Imperial Scribe Censor.

sentences.zh: 詔問時務所當先者，璧上六事，大略言減冗食，備選鋒，緩疑似以慎刑，擇公廉以檢吏，屯戍革朘削之弊，權貴嚴請托之科。

translations.literal: An edict asked what current affairs ought to come first. Bi submitted six matters, broadly speaking: reduce redundant consumption, prepare picked vanguard troops, ease doubtful cases to be cautious in punishments, select the fair and incorrupt to inspect officials, reform the abuses of encampment graft, and strictly penalize patronage among the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked what current affairs should come first, Bi submitted six proposals: reduce redundant spending, prepare elite vanguard forces, ease doubtful cases to make punishments more cautious, select fair and incorrupt officials to inspect the bureaucracy, reform abuses in military encampments, and strictly penalize patronage among the powerful.

sentences.zh: 又條自治之策四，謂別賢佞，信賞罰，聽覽以通下情，貶損以謹天戒。

translations.literal: He also set forth four policies for self-governance: distinguish the worthy from the depraved, trust rewards and punishments, listen and review to open lower feelings, and reduce extravagance to heed Heaven's warnings.
translations.idiomatic: He also set forth four policies for self-governance: distinguish the worthy from the wicked, trust rewards and punishments, listen and review to learn what the people feel, and reduce extravagance to heed Heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 詔以東方饑饉，盜賊並起，以御史中丞完顏伯嘉為宣慰使，監察御史道遠從行。

translations.literal: An edict, because the east suffered famine and bandits rose together, appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief Wanyan Bojia as Pacification Commissioner, with Investigating Censor Dao Yuan accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: Because famine struck the east and bandits rose together, an edict appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief Wanyan Bojia Pacification Commissioner, with Investigating Censor Dao Yuan accompanying him.

sentences.zh: 道遠發永城令簿奸贓，伯嘉與令有違，付令有司，釋簿不問，燕語之際，又許參佐克忠等台職。

translations.literal: Dao Yuan exposed the magistrate and clerk of Yongcheng for treachery and embezzlement. Bojia had a dispute with the magistrate, handed the magistrate to the relevant offices, and released the clerk without inquiry. At a leisurely conversation he also promised the aides Ke Zhong and others censorial posts.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Yuan exposed the magistrate and clerk of Yongcheng for corruption. Bojia sided with the magistrate, handed the magistrate to the authorities, and released the clerk without inquiry. In private conversation he also promised aides such as Ke Zhong posts on the censorate.

sentences.zh: 璧皆劾之，伯嘉竟得罪去。

translations.literal: Bi impeached them all, and Bojia in the end was punished and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Bi impeached them all, and Bojia was eventually punished and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 初，諜者告歸德行樞密院言，河朔叛軍有竊謀南渡者，行院事胡土門、都水監使毛花輦易其人，不為備。

translations.literal: Earlier a spy reported to the Guiding Military Commission that Heshuo rebel troops secretly plotted to cross south. The commission administrator Hu Tumen and Director of Waterworks Mao Huanian replaced the informant and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a spy reported to the Guiding Military Commission that rebel troops from Heshuo were secretly plotting to cross the river south. Commission administrator Hu Tumen and Director of Waterworks Mao Huanian replaced the informant and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 一日，紅衲數百聯筏南渡，殘下邑而去。

translations.literal: One day several hundred Red-Robed men linked rafts and crossed south, ravaged lower towns, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: One day several hundred Red-Robed rebels linked rafts and crossed south, ravaged nearby towns, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 命璧鞫之。

translations.literal: Bi was ordered to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 璧以二將托疾營私，聞寇弛備，且來不戰、去不追，在法皆當斬。

translations.literal: Bi held that the two generals, feigning illness to pursue private gain, heard of bandits yet relaxed preparations, and when they came did not fight and when they left did not pursue—all by law deserving execution.
translations.idiomatic: Bi held that the two generals had feigned illness to pursue private gain, heard of the raid yet relaxed their guard, and neither fought when the enemy came nor pursued when they left. By law all three offenses deserved execution.

sentences.zh: 或以為言：「二將皆寵臣，而都水者貲累巨萬，若求援禁近，必從輕典。

translations.literal: Someone said to him: 'Both generals are favored ministers, and the Director of Waterworks has wealth accumulated to tens of thousands. If they seek aid from those near the forbidden precinct, they will surely receive lenient punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him: 'Both generals are favored courtiers, and the Director of Waterworks has amassed wealth in the tens of thousands. If they appeal to those close to the throne, they will surely receive lenient punishment.

sentences.zh: 君徒結怨權貴，果何益耶？」

translations.literal: You will only make enemies of the powerful and noble—what benefit will there truly be?'
translations.idiomatic: You will only make enemies of the powerful. What good will that do you?'

sentences.zh: 璧歎曰：「睢陽行闕，東籓重兵所宿，門廷之寇且不能禦，有大於此者，複何望乎！」

translations.literal: Bi sighed and said: 'Suiyang is the traveling palace, where the eastern defense's heavy troops are stationed. Bandits at the gate cannot even be repelled—if there is something greater than this, what can one hope for!'
translations.idiomatic: Bi sighed and said: 'Suiyang is the traveling palace where the eastern defense's main forces are stationed. If bandits at the gate cannot even be repelled, what hope is there for anything greater!'

sentences.zh: 即具所擬聞。

translations.literal: He immediately set forth his draft and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted his proposed sentence.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 關中旱，詔璧與吏部侍郎畏忻審理冤獄。

translations.literal: Guanzhong suffered drought. An edict ordered Bi and Vice Minister of Personnel Wei Xin to examine and settle wrongful cases.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck Guanzhong, an edict ordered Bi and Vice Minister of Personnel Wei Xin to review wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 時河中帥阿虎帶及僚屬十數人皆以棄城罪當死，系同州獄待報。

translations.literal: At that time the Hezhong commander A Hudai and more than ten subordinates were all, for the crime of abandoning the city, deserving death, imprisoned in Tongzhou awaiting report.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Hezhong commander A Hudai and more than ten of his subordinates faced death for abandoning their city and were held in Tongzhou prison awaiting sentence.

sentences.zh: 同州官僚承望風旨，問璧何以處之，璧曰：「河中今日重地，朝議擬為駐蹕之所，若失此則河南、陝西有脣亡之憂。

translations.literal: The Tongzhou officials, following the prevailing wind, asked how Bi would deal with it. Bi said: 'Hezhong today is a vital place; court deliberation plans it as a place for the emperor's halt. If this is lost, then Henan and Shaanxi will have the worry of lips perishing when the teeth grow cold.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongzhou officials, reading the prevailing wind, asked how Bi would handle the case. Bi said: 'Hezhong is a vital post today, and the court plans to make it a place for the emperor to halt. If we lose it, Henan and Shaanxi will face the danger that comes when the lips are gone and the teeth grow cold.

sentences.zh: 以彼宗室勳貴故使鎮之，平居無事竭民膏血為浚築計，一旦有警乃遽焚蕩而去，此而不誅，三尺法無用矣。」

translations.literal: Because they are imperial clansmen of meritorious nobility they were sent to guard it. In ordinary times, with nothing happening, they exhaust the people's lifeblood for dredging and building plans; once alarm comes they suddenly burn and ravage and leave. If this is not punished, the three-foot law is useless.'
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen of noble merit were sent to guard it. In peacetime they drained the people's blood for dredging and fortification, and at the first alarm they burned everything and fled. If this goes unpunished, the law is worthless.'

sentences.zh: 竟以無冤上之。

translations.literal: In the end he reported upward that there was no injustice.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he reported that there was no injustice in the case.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，出為歸德治中。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he went out as Administrator of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he was posted as Administrator of Guide.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改同知保靜軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Associate Military Commissioner of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Associate Military Commissioner of the Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 又改同知集慶軍節度使，到官即上章乞骸骨，進一官致仕。

translations.literal: He was again changed to Associate Military Commissioner of Jiqing Army. On reaching office he immediately submitted a memorial begging to retire on old bones, was advanced one rank, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Associate Military Commissioner of the Jiqing Army. On taking office he immediately submitted a memorial requesting retirement, was promoted one rank, and retired.

sentences.zh: 正大九年，河南破，北歸，又數年卒，年七十有九。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengda Henan was broken; he returned north, and after several more years died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhengda, when Henan fell, he returned north and died several years later at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 李獻甫

translations.literal: Li Xianfu
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianfu

sentences.zh: 李獻甫，字欽用，獻能從弟也。

translations.literal: Li Xianfu, styled Qinyong, was a younger cousin of Xianneng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianfu, whose style name was Qinyong, was a younger cousin of Li Xianneng.

sentences.zh: 博通書傳，尤精《左氏》及地理學。

translations.literal: He was broadly versed in books and traditions, especially skilled in the Zuo Tradition and geography.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned in the classics, especially skilled in the Zuo Tradition and geography.

sentences.zh: 為人有幹局，心所到則絕人遠甚，故時人稱其精神滿腹。

translations.literal: As a man he had capacity and scope; where his mind reached he far surpassed others, and therefore people of the time called him one whose spirit filled his belly.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of great capacity and force of mind, far surpassing others in whatever he undertook, and contemporaries said his spirit filled his whole being.

sentences.zh: 興定五年登進士第，曆咸陽簿，辟行台令史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xingding he passed the jinshi examination, served as clerk of Xianyang, and was recruited as clerk of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Xingding, served as clerk of Xianyang, and was recruited as a clerk of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正大初，夏使來請和，朝廷以翰林待制馮延登往議，時獻甫為書表官，從行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengda, Xia envoys came to request peace. The court sent Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting Feng Yandeng to negotiate; at that time Xianfu was document officer and accompanied the mission.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengda, Western Xia envoys came to seek peace. The court sent Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting Feng Yandeng to negotiate, with Xianfu serving as document officer on the mission.

sentences.zh: 夏使有口辯，延登不能折，往復數日不定，至以歲幣為言，獻甫不能平，從旁進曰：「夏國與我和好百年，今雖易君臣之名為兄弟之國，使兄輸幣，寧有據耶？」

translations.literal: The Xia envoy was skilled in debate; Yandeng could not refute him. Back and forth for several days they could not settle it, until they spoke of annual tribute. Xianfu could not remain calm and advanced from the side: 'The Xia state has been at peace with us for a hundred years. Though we have changed the names of ruler and subject to a brotherly state, for the elder brother to pay tribute—can there be grounds for this?'
translations.idiomatic: The Xia envoy was a skilled debater whom Yandeng could not refute. Talks went back and forth for days without resolution until tribute payments came up. Xianfu could not contain himself and spoke from the side: 'The Xia state has been at peace with us for a hundred years. Though we have changed the names of ruler and subject to those of brother states, can there be any grounds for the elder brother to pay tribute?'

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「兄弟且不論。

translations.literal: The envoy said: 'Let us not discuss brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said: 'Let us set aside the question of brothers.

sentences.zh: 宋歲輸吾國幣二十五萬疋，典故具在，君獨不知耶？

translations.literal: Song annually pays our state two hundred fifty thousand bolts of silk; the precedents are all in place—are you alone ignorant of this?
translations.idiomatic: Song pays our state two hundred fifty thousand bolts of silk each year. The precedents are all on record. Are you alone ignorant of this?

sentences.zh: 金朝必欲修舊好，非此例不可。」

translations.literal: If the Jin court must restore the old peace, it cannot be done without this precedent.'
translations.idiomatic: If the Jin court wishes to restore the old peace, it cannot be done without following this precedent.'

sentences.zh: 獻甫作色曰：「使者尚忍言耶？

translations.literal: Xianfu changed color and said: 'Envoy, how can you still bear to speak of this?
translations.idiomatic: Xianfu flushed with anger and said: 'Envoy, how can you still speak of such a thing?

sentences.zh: 宋以歲幣餌君家而賜之姓，岸然以君父自居，夏國君臣無一悟者，誠謂使者當以為諱，乃今公言之。

translations.literal: Song used annual tribute to bait your house and bestowed a surname; they stood aloof and took the position of lord and father. Not one among Xia's ruler and ministers has awakened to this. I truly thought the envoy ought to treat it as taboo—yet today you speak of it openly.
translations.idiomatic: Song used annual tribute to bait your rulers and then bestowed a surname on them, standing aloof as lord and father over you. Not one among Xia's ruler and ministers has understood this shame. I thought an envoy ought to treat it as taboo, yet today you speak of it openly.

sentences.zh: 使者果能主此議，以從賜姓之例，弊邑雖歲捐五十萬，獻甫請以身任之。」

translations.literal: If the envoy can truly uphold this proposal and follow the precedent of receiving a bestowed surname, though our humble state yearly donate five hundred thousand, Xianfu asks to bear it in person.'
translations.idiomatic: If you can truly uphold this proposal and follow the precedent of receiving a bestowed surname, then though our state must pay five hundred thousand a year, I myself will answer for it.'

sentences.zh: 夏使語塞，和議乃定。

translations.literal: The Xia envoy was speechless, and the peace agreement was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia envoy was left speechless, and the peace agreement was settled.

sentences.zh: 後朝廷錄其功，授慶陽總帥府經歷官。

translations.literal: Later the court recorded his merit and appointed him Administrator of the Qingyang Commander-in-Chief's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court recognized his merit and appointed him Administrator of the Qingyang Commander-in-Chief's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋辟長安令。

translations.literal: Shortly he was recruited as Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 京兆行台所在，供億甚繁，獻甫處之常若有餘，縣民賴之以安。

translations.literal: The Jingzhao Branch Secretariat was located there and supplies were very burdensome. Xianfu handled it as if he always had surplus, and the county people relied on him for security.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhao Branch Secretariat was located there and demands on the county were heavy. Xianfu handled them as though he always had surplus, and the people relied on him for security.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Secretariat Clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a Secretariat Clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 天興元年，充行六部員外郎，守備之策時相倚任之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxing he filled the post of Vice Director of the Traveling Six Ministries; on defense strategy the chief ministers at the time relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing he served as Vice Director of the Traveling Six Ministries, and the chief ministers relied heavily on him for defense strategy.

sentences.zh: 以功遷鎮南軍節度副使，兼右警巡使，死于蔡州之難，年四十。

translations.literal: For merit he was moved to Vice Military Commissioner of Zhennan Army, concurrently Right Patrol Commissioner, and died in the calamity at Caizhou, aged forty.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Vice Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army and Right Patrol Commissioner. He died in the disaster at Caizhou at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 所著文章號《天倪集》，留汴京。

translations.literal: His collected writings were titled Collection of Heaven's Margin and were left in Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings, titled Collection of Heaven's Margin, were left behind in Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 獻甫死，其家亦破，同年華陰王元禮購得之，傳於世。

translations.literal: When Xianfu died his family was also ruined. His examination-year fellow Wang Yuanli of Huayin purchased it and transmitted it to the world.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianfu's death his family was ruined as well. His examination-year fellow Wang Yuanli of Huayin purchased the work and preserved it for posterity.

sentences.zh: 雷淵，字希顏，一字季默，應州渾源人。

translations.literal: Lei Yuan, styled Xiyan, with another style Jimo, was a man of Hunyuan in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Yuan, whose style names were Xiyan and Jimo, came from Hunyuan in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父思，名進士，仕至同知北京轉運使，注《易》行於世。

translations.literal: His father Si, a famous jinshi, served up to Associate Commissioner of the Beijing Circuit Transport Commission. His commentary on the Changes circulates in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His father Si, a renowned jinshi, rose to Associate Commissioner of the Beijing Circuit Transport Commission. His commentary on the Changes circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 淵庶出，年最幼，諸兄不齒。

translations.literal: Yuan was born of a concubine, the youngest in years; his elder brothers did not regard him as equal.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was born of a concubine and was the youngest. His elder brothers looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 父歿，不能安於家，乃發憤入太學。

translations.literal: When his father died he could not rest at home and, in indignant resolve, entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he could not remain at home and entered the Imperial Academy in indignant resolve.

sentences.zh: 衣弊履穿，坐榻無席，自以跣露，恆兀坐讀書，不迎送賓客，人皆以為倨。

translations.literal: His clothes were worn and his shoes torn; his sitting couch had no mat. Because he went barefoot, he always sat upright reading books, not greeting or seeing off guests. People all thought him arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: His clothes were worn and his shoes torn, his couch had no mat, and he went barefoot. He always sat upright reading and never greeted or saw off guests. People took him for arrogant.

sentences.zh: 其友商衡每為辯之，且周恤焉。

translations.literal: His friend Shang Heng often argued on his behalf and also gave him relief.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Shang Heng often spoke up for him and gave him support.

sentences.zh: 後從李之純游，遂知名。

translations.literal: Later he followed Li Zhichun in study and thereupon became known.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied under Li Zhichun and became well known.

sentences.zh: 登至甯元年詞賦進士甲科，調涇州錄事，坐高庭玉獄，幾死。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhi'ning he passed the cifu jinshi in the first rank and was assigned as Recorder of Jingzhou. He was implicated in Gao Tingyu's case and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhi'ning he passed the cifu jinshi examination in the top rank and was assigned as Recorder of Jingzhou. He was implicated in Gao Tingyu's case and nearly died.

sentences.zh: 後改東平，河朔重兵所在，驕將悍卒倚外敵為重，自行台以下皆摩撫之，淵出入軍中，偃然不為屈。

translations.literal: Later he was changed to Dongping, where Heshuo's heavy troops were stationed. Proud generals and fierce soldiers relied on foreign enemies for weight; from the Branch Secretariat down all soothed them. Yuan went in and out of the armies, unbending and not submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posted to Dongping, where Heshuo's main forces were stationed. Proud generals and fierce soldiers relied on foreign enemies for leverage, and everyone from the Branch Secretariat down indulged them. Yuan moved in and out of the armies unbowed.

sentences.zh: 不數月，閭巷間多畫淵像，雖大將不敢以新進書生遇之。

translations.literal: Within a few months many in lanes and alleys painted Yuan's portrait; even great generals did not dare treat this newly advanced scholar-official lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months portraits of Yuan appeared in the streets, and even senior generals did not dare treat the newly advanced scholar lightly.

sentences.zh: 尋遷東阿令，轉徐州觀察判官。

translations.literal: Shortly he was moved to Magistrate of Dong'e, then transferred to Judicial Officer of the Xuzhou Observation Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Magistrate of Dong'e, then transferred to Judicial Officer of the Xuzhou Observation Commission.

sentences.zh: 興定末，召為英王府文學兼記室參軍，轉應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: At the end of Xingding he was summoned as Literary Scholar of the Prince of Ying's household, concurrently Secretary of the household staff, then moved to Hanlin Attendant for Documentation.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xingding era he was summoned as Literary Scholar of the Prince of Ying's household and Secretary of the household staff, then made Hanlin Attendant for Documentation.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，言五事稱旨，又彈劾不避權貴，出巡郡邑所至有威譽，奸豪不法者立箠殺之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor. Five matters he spoke met with approval; he also impeached without avoiding the powerful and noble. Touring prefectures and districts, wherever he arrived he had awe and reputation, and treacherous bullies who broke the law he immediately clubbed to death.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Investigating Censor. Five proposals he made pleased the emperor, and he impeached without fear of the powerful. Touring the prefectures, he won awe wherever he went and immediately clubbed to death any outlaw bully he found.

sentences.zh: 至蔡州，杖殺五百人，時號曰「雷半千」。

translations.literal: At Caizhou he beat five hundred men to death; people at the time called him "Lei Five Hundred."
translations.idiomatic: At Caizhou he beat five hundred men to death, and people called him "Lei Five Hundred."

sentences.zh: 坐此為人所訟，罷去。

translations.literal: Because of this he was sued by others and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，用宰相侯摯薦，起為太學博士、南京轉運司戶籍判官，遷翰林修撰。

translations.literal: After a long time, on Chancellor Hou Zhi's recommendation, he was raised as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Household Registration Judicial Officer of the Nanjing Transport Commission, then moved to Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval, on Chancellor Hou Zhi's recommendation, he was recalled as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Household Registration Judicial Officer on the Nanjing Transport Commission, then promoted to Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 一夕暴卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: One evening he died suddenly, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: One evening he died suddenly at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 正大庚寅倒回穀之役，淵嘗上書破朝臣孤注之論，引援深切，灼然易見，主兵者沮之，策竟不行。

translations.literal: In the gengyin year of Zhengda, in the campaign at Daohuigu, Yuan once submitted a memorial refuting the court gentlemen's wager-all theory. His citations were deep and cutting, clear and easy to see, but those in charge of the armies obstructed it and the plan in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: During the gengyin year of Zhengda, in the campaign at Daohuigu, Yuan submitted a memorial refuting the court's all-or-nothing strategy. His argument was penetrating and clear, but the men in charge of the armies blocked it and the plan was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 為人軀幹雄偉，髯張口哆，顏渥丹，眼如望洋，遇不平則疾惡之氣見於顏間，或嚼齒大罵不休，雖痛自懲創，然亦不能變也。

translations.literal: As a man his frame was heroic and grand, beard bristling and mouth gaping, face rich and red, eyes like gazing at the ocean. When he met injustice, fierce hatred showed on his face; sometimes he ground his teeth and cursed loudly without cease. Though he severely punished himself, he still could not change.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of heroic build, bristling beard and gaping mouth, ruddy face and eyes like the open sea. When he met injustice, fierce hatred showed on his face. Sometimes he ground his teeth and cursed without cease. Though he punished himself severely, he could not change.

sentences.zh: 為文章詩喜新奇。

translations.literal: In essays and poetry he delighted in the new and strange.
translations.idiomatic: In essays and poetry he delighted in the new and strange.

sentences.zh: 善結交，凡當塗貴要與布衣名士無不往來。

translations.literal: He was skilled at making friends; whether those in power and favor or commoner gentlemen of renown, there were none with whom he did not associate.
translations.idiomatic: He made friends easily, associating alike with men in power and with renowned scholars in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 居京師，賓客踵門未嘗去舍，家無餘貲，及待賓客甚豐腆。

translations.literal: Living in the capital, guests followed one another to his door and never left his house. The family had no surplus wealth, yet in receiving guests he was very lavish.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital guests crowded his door and never seemed to leave. His household had no surplus wealth, yet he entertained guests lavishly.

sentences.zh: 蒞官喜立名，初登第攝遂平縣事，年少氣稅，擊豪右，發奸伏，一邑大震，稱為神明。

translations.literal: On taking office he liked to establish a name. When he first passed the examinations and acted in Suiping county affairs, young in years and bold in spirit, he struck powerful families and exposed hidden wrongdoing. The whole district was greatly shaken and called him divine.
translations.idiomatic: In office he liked to make a name for himself. When he first passed the examinations and acted in Suiping county affairs, young and bold, he struck down powerful families and exposed hidden crimes. The whole district was shaken and called him divine.

sentences.zh: 嘗擅笞州魁吏，州檄召之不應，罷去。

translations.literal: He once on his own authority beat the leading clerk of the prefecture. The prefecture dispatched a summons and he did not respond; he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He once beat the leading clerk of the prefecture on his own authority. When the prefecture summoned him he did not respond and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後凡居一職輒震耀，亦坐此不達。

translations.literal: Later, whenever he held one post he would shine brilliantly, yet because of this he also did not reach high advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in every post he held he made a brilliant mark, yet because of this he never rose high.

sentences.zh: 程震，字威卿，東勝人。

translations.literal: Cheng Zhen, styled Weiqing, was a man of Dongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhen, whose style name was Weiqing, came from Dongsheng.

sentences.zh: 與其兄鼎俱擢第。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Ding both were selected in the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Ding both passed the examinations.

sentences.zh: 震入仕有能聲。

translations.literal: Zhen, on entering office, had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen earned a reputation for ability from the start of his career.

sentences.zh: 興定初，詔百官舉縣令，震得陳留，治為河南第一，召拜監察御史，彈劾無所撓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingding an edict ordered all officials to recommend county magistrates. Zhen obtained Chenliu; his governance was first in Henan. He was summoned and appointed Investigating Censor, impeaching without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xingding an edict ordered all officials to recommend county magistrates. Zhen was appointed to Chenliu and his governance ranked first in Henan. He was summoned and made Investigating Censor, impeaching without fear.

sentences.zh: 時皇子荊王為宰相，家僮輩席勢侵民，震以法劾之，奏曰：「荊王以陛下之子，任天下之重。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial son, the Prince of Jing, was chancellor. His household servants, relying on power, encroached on the people. Zhen impeached them by law and memorialized: 'The Prince of Jing, as Your Majesty's son, bears the weight of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Jing, an imperial son, served as chancellor. His household servants abused their master's power to oppress the people. Zhen impeached them by law and memorialized: 'The Prince of Jing, as Your Majesty's son, bears the weight of the realm.

sentences.zh: 不能上贊君父，同濟艱難。

translations.literal: He cannot above assist ruler and father and together relieve hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he cannot assist his sovereign father above or share in relieving the state's hardships.

sentences.zh: 顧乃專恃權勢，蔑棄典禮，開納貨賂，進退官吏。

translations.literal: Instead he relies solely on power and influence, despises and abandons canonical ritual, openly receives bribes, and advances and dismisses officials.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he relies solely on power, scorns proper ritual, openly accepts bribes, and advances or dismisses officials at will.

sentences.zh: 縱令奴隸侵漁細民，名為和市，其實脅取。

translations.literal: He lets slaves encroach on and plunder common people, calling it harmonized markets when in fact it is coercion and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: He lets his slaves prey on commoners under the name of official markets when in fact they extort by force.

sentences.zh: 諸所不法不可枚舉。

translations.literal: All his unlawful acts cannot be counted and listed.
translations.idiomatic: His unlawful acts are too many to list.

sentences.zh: 陛下不能正家，而欲正天下，難矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty cannot rectify the family yet wishes to rectify all under Heaven—this is difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty cannot set your own household in order, how can you hope to set the realm in order? That will be difficult indeed.'

sentences.zh: 於是，上責荊王，出內府銀以償物直，杖大奴尤不法者數人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor reproached the Prince of Jing, issued silver from the inner treasury to pay the value of goods, and beat several chief slaves who were especially unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon rebuked the Prince of Jing, paid compensation from the inner treasury for seized goods, and had several of the worst offenders among his chief slaves beaten.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐為故吏所訟，罷官。

translations.literal: Before long, because he was sued by a former subordinate, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was impeached by a former subordinate and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘。

translations.literal: After more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later,

sentences.zh: 嘔血卒。

translations.literal: he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: he vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 震為人剛直有材幹，忘身徇國，不少私與。

translations.literal: Zhen as a man was firm, upright, and capable; he forgot his person and followed the state, granting little in private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was a man of firm uprightness and real ability who forgot himself in service to the state and showed little favoritism in private dealings.

sentences.zh: 及為御史，台綱大振，以故小人側目者眾，不能久留於朝，士論惜之。

translations.literal: When he became censor, the censorate's standards were greatly revived. Because of this many petty men looked askance at him; he could not long remain at court, and scholar opinion regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: As censor he revived the censorate's authority, and for that reason many petty men watched him with hostility. He could not long remain at court, and scholars regretted his loss.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：韓玉、馮璧、李獻甫、雷淵，皆金季豪傑之士也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Han Yu, Feng Bi, Li Xianfu, and Lei Yuan were all heroic and outstanding gentlemen of the late Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Han Yu, Feng Bi, Li Xianfu, and Lei Yuan were all heroic figures of the late Jin.

sentences.zh: 邠、涇之變，玉募兵旬日而得萬人。

translations.literal: At the upheaval in Bin and Jing, Yu recruited troops and within ten days obtained ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis at Bin and Jing, Yu raised ten thousand troops within ten days.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔之兇暴，璧以王度繩之，卒不敢動。

translations.literal: Yawuta's ferocity and violence—Bi bound him with royal measure, and in the end he did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: When Yawuta turned violent, Bi restrained him by royal authority, and in the end he did not dare resist.

sentences.zh: 夏人援宋例以邀歲幣，獻甫以宋賜夏姓一事折之，夏使語塞而和議定。

translations.literal: The Xia people cited Song precedent to demand annual tribute. Xianfu refuted them with the matter of Song bestowing a surname on Xia; the Xia envoy was speechless and the peace agreement was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Xia cited Song precedent to demand annual tribute. Xianfu refuted them with the shame of Song bestowing a surname on Xia. The Xia envoy was left speechless and peace was settled.

sentences.zh: 淵為御史，權貴斂避，古之國士何加焉。

translations.literal: Yuan as censor made the powerful and noble restrain themselves and withdraw—what could be added to the state gentlemen of antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: As censor Yuan made the powerful shrink back. What more could be asked of the great men of old?

sentences.zh: 玉以疑見冤，璧、淵疾惡太甚，議者以酷譏之，瑕豈可以掩瑜哉。

translations.literal: Yu was wronged through suspicion; Bi and Yuan hated evil too greatly—deliberators mocked them as cruel. Can a flaw cover the jade?
translations.idiomatic: Yu was wronged through suspicion. Bi and Yuan hated evil too fiercely, and critics called them cruel. Yet can a flaw hide the jade?

sentences.zh: 程震劾荊抵罪，比蹤馮、雷，然亦以群小齟齬而死，直士之不容於世也久矣。

translations.literal: Cheng Zhen impeached the Prince of Jing and brought guilt upon him, comparable in track to Feng and Lei, yet he also died through petty men's friction. That upright gentlemen are not tolerated in the world has been long.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhen impeached the Prince of Jing and brought him to account, in the same mold as Feng and Lei, yet he too died through petty men's hostility. That upright men find no place in the world has been true for a long time.

sentences.zh: 籲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!
